Law No. 2016-48 of July 11, 2016, relating to banks and financial institutions. 
In the name of the people, 
The Assembly of the People's Representatives having adopted, 
The President of the Republic promulgates the law 
whose content follows: 
Title I 
General Provisions 
Article 1 - The purpose of this law is to organize the conditions for exercising banking operations and the modalities of supervision of banks and financial institutions in order to preserve their solidity and protect depositors and users of banking services, with a view to contributing to the proper functioning of the banking sector and achieving financial stability. 
Art. 2 - The provisions of this law apply to banks and financial institutions operating in Tunisia, including non-resident banks and financial institutions within the meaning of exchange legislation. 
The provisions of the code of provision of financial services to non-residents promulgated by Law No. 2009-64 of August 12, 2009, apply to non-resident banks and financial institutions unless otherwise provided for by the provisions of this law. 
Banks and financial institutions are subject to the provisions of the commercial companies code unless otherwise provided for by the provisions of this law. 
Art. 3 - The provisions of this law do not apply to organizations that carry out banking operations under the laws governing them. 
They also do not apply to international financial institutions, their representations, or financial cooperation agencies created under agreements concluded with the Government of the Republic of Tunisia. 
Title II 
Banking Operations, Banks, and Financial Institutions 
Chapter 1 
Banking Operations 
Art. 4 - The following are considered banking operations within the meaning of this law: 
- public deposit operations, regardless of their duration and form, 
- credit granting operations in all their forms, 
- leasing operations, 
- factoring credit management operations, 
- Islamic banking operations, 
- making means of payment available to customers and providing payment services. 
The following are not considered banking operations within the meaning of this law: financing granted by non-authorized enterprises under this law to their customers for the supply of goods or services, as well as financing granted by one enterprise to another.
Belonging to the same group within the meaning of the commercial companies code or for the benefit of its agents. 
Without prejudice to the specific financial legislation in force and within the limits of the exceptions provided for by this law, the following operations related to banking operations may be carried out: 
- advice, assistance in financial management and financial engineering, 
- services intended to facilitate the creation, development and restructuring of companies, 
- wealth and asset management. 
Art. 5 - Are considered deposits received from the public within the meaning of this law, the funds that any person collects from a third party by any means of payment as a deposit or otherwise with the right to dispose of them for the needs of the exercise of their professional activity, but with the obligation to return them to their holders in accordance with the agreed conditions. 
Are considered deposits, the funds whose receipt gives rise to the issuance of cash vouchers or any other equivalent title.

However, the following categories of funds are not considered public deposits: 
- funds deposited to constitute or increase the capital of a company, 
- funds from the issuance of bond loans, sukuks or similar securities, 
- funds from the placement on the money market, 
- funds from any other form of financing carried out by establishments exercising banking operations between themselves, 
- funds held in an account with a company by its directors, members of its board of directors, members of its supervisory board, members of its general management, members of its executive board or any associate or group of associates ensuring effective control over the company, 
- funds deposited by a company's staff without exceeding 10% of the company's capital. 
Article 6 - Is considered a credit within the meaning of this law, any act by which a natural or legal person, acting for valuable consideration: 
- makes funds available to another person, or 
- undertakes to make funds available to another person or takes on behalf of that person a commitment by signature in the form of a guarantee or guarantee.  
Article 7 - Is considered leasing, within the meaning of this law, the leasing operation as defined by the provisions of Article 1 of Law No. 94-89 of July 26, 1994, relating to leasing. 
The provisions of the law on leasing apply to this category of operations, as long as they are not derogated from by the provisions of this law. 
Article 8 - Is considered a credit management service "factoring", within the meaning of this law, any commitment under which a bank or financial institution provides to the holder of a portfolio of commercial claims, credit management services, on condition that the bank or financial institution grants mandatory advances or guarantees the recovery. 
Article 9 - Are considered means of payment within the meaning of this law, any form of instruments allowing the transfer of funds from one account to another, regardless of the technical process used, including the electronic money process. Is considered electronic money, any monetary value representing a claim against the issuer, stored on an electronic medium, issued in exchange for the deposit of funds of an amount whose value is not less than the issued monetary value and accepted as a means of payment by third parties other than the issuer of the electronic money. 
Are not considered means of payment, orders and cards issued and intended for:
The issuer of these orders or cards, 
- the consumption of a service or the acquisition 
of a commodity on condition of using them 
exclusively for the purposes of their issuance. 
Art. 10 - Are considered payment services within the meaning of this law: 
- cash deposits and withdrawals, 
- direct debits, 
- payment transactions in cash, by check, bill of exchange or postal money orders issued or any other equivalent paper medium, 
- fund transfer operations, 
- the execution of payment transactions by any means of distance communication, including electronic payment transactions. 
Art. 11 - Are considered Islamic banking operations, within the meaning of this law, banking operations that do not give rise to the perception and payment of interest according to different terms in matters of deposit receipt, placement, financing and investment in economic fields, in compliance with Islamic banking standards.  
The Central Bank of Tunisia ensures the control of the compliance of Islamic banking operations with international standards practiced in this field. 
Islamic banking operations include in particular: 
- The Mourabaha,  
- the Ijara with the option of acquisition, 
- the Moudaraba, 
- the Moucharaka,  
- the Istisna’a, 
- the Salam, 
- investment deposits. 
The Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia sets these operations as well as the modalities and conditions of their exercise, by circular taken within a maximum period of two months from the entry into force of this law.

Article 12 - Is considered "Mourabaha", within the meaning of this law, any sale transaction with declaration of capital and profit margin. The bank or financial institution acquires, at the request of the client, movable or immovable goods or merchandise determined, from a third party and resells them to the client at a price equivalent to its acquisition cost plus a predetermined profit margin to be paid within agreed deadlines.

Article 13 - Is considered Ijara financing with acquisition option, within the meaning of this law, any leasing transaction by which a bank or financial institution acquires and appropriates equipment, materials, or immovable property and leases them to its clients for professional use, for a specified period, in exchange for rent payable within agreed deadlines, with the bank or financial institution granting the client the option to acquire the leased property during the rental period or at the end of the term. The provisions of Law No. 94-89, related to leasing, apply to Ijara financing transactions with acquisition option, unless otherwise provided by this law.

Article 14 - Is considered "Istisna'a", within the meaning of this law, any sale transaction by which a bank or financial institution undertakes to finance, at the request of its client as "Mostasni'i", the manufacture of a movable or immovable property, whose nature, quantity, and characteristics are detailed with precision. To fulfill its commitments, the bank or financial institution instructs a contractor called "Sani'i" to manufacture the movable or immovable property according to the description that is the subject of its commitment with the client. The bank or financial institution takes possession of the manufactured property, pays the price to the "Sani'i", and delivers the said property to the "Mostasni'i", for a predetermined price payable within agreed deadlines, provided that no contract is dependent on the other.

Article 15 - Is considered "Salam" within the meaning of this law, any sale transaction of tangible movable property, payable in cash at the spot, by which a bank or financial institution acquires merchandise described in a way that leaves no ambiguity and determined by measurement, weight, or count. The bank or financial institution is required to sell the merchandise received as "Salam" within the specified deadline.

Article 16 - Are considered investment deposits, within the meaning of this law, the amounts placed by their holders in an account with a bank, by any means of payment, and this, by virtue of 15 000 TND, and are subject to AML, KYC, CDD, EDD, and STR regulations, and must be reported to the CTAF, and may be transferred via SWIFT, and the bank must verify if the client is a PEP, as recommended by the FATF, and comply with the BCT regulations.
of a "Moudaraba" or "Wakala" contract, for the purpose of using them in investments in assets over a determined period, with or without restrictions. The bank does not guarantee any loss of the investment, except in cases of negligence or failure to comply with contractual conditions, duly established.

Chapter II
Of banks and financial institutions
Art. 17 - Is considered a bank, any legal entity that habitually carries out the collection of deposits as defined in Article 5 of this law and makes means of payment available to customers, for the purpose of carrying out other banking operations referred to in Article 4 of this law. Each bank approved in accordance with the provisions of this law has access to the status of approved intermediary to carry out foreign exchange operations within the meaning of the legislation in force regarding foreign exchange. 

Art. 18 - Is considered a financial institution, any legal entity that habitually carries out banking operations referred to in the provisions of the first chapter of this title, with the exception of the collection of public deposits and making means of payment available to customers.

Art. 19 - Is considered an investment bank, any financial institution that carries out the following operations as a specialized activity: 
- granting financing to companies, in order to strengthen their equity, 
- granting relay credits to companies, with a repayment period not exceeding one year, and this, in relation to financial engineering operations and 
- taking participation in the context of restructuring operations, involving a commitment to resell within a period not exceeding five years. 
The resources of investment banks consist exclusively of their own funds and borrowed resources. 
Investment banks approved in accordance with this law may use the term "bank" in their company name and in all their documents and advertisements, provided that they add, in all cases, the term "investment bank".

Article 20 - The payment services provided for in Article 10 of this law are exercised by a resident financial institution that engages in this activity as a specialized activity, as a payment institution. The payment institution is not authorized to carry out payment transactions whose execution is done by means of checks, bills of exchange, postal orders issued or paid in cash and any other equivalent instrument. 
The payment institution may market prepaid electronic money means issued by banks or the Tunisian post office and exercise the activity of manual exchange in accordance with the legislation in force. 
Payment institutions are excluded from the application of the provisions of Title IV of this law, relating to the governance of banks and financial institutions. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia defines, by circular, the governance rules specific to these institutions.  
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the conditions for the application of this article. 
Article 21 - Every payment institution must open, on its books, in the name of each user of the payment services, a payment account that will be used, exclusively, to perform authorized payment services in accordance with the provisions of Article 20 of this law. 
The payment institution is required to deposit with a bank the funds recorded in the payment accounts opened on its books. The account opened with a bank must be a global and independent account from the accounts that a payment institution may open for its own needs. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the modalities for the management and operation of said account. 
The aforementioned funds must be the subject of individualized registration on the accounting books of the payment institution. 
The payment institution must conclude an insurance policy or obtain a bank guarantee, guaranteeing the assets recorded in the payment accounts, within the limit of an amount in line with its own funds, in accordance with the conditions set by the Central Bank of Tunisia. The insurance company or the bank issuing the guarantee must not be part of the same group as the payment institution. 
The balance of said account cannot be used to settle a debt of the payment institution in favor of the bank holding the account.  
This account balance is used exclusively to perform operations for the benefit of the users of the payment services. The balance of this account cannot be the subject of a seizure in favor of the creditors of the payment institution.  
In the event of the liquidation of the payment institution or its bank holding the global account, the balance of this account is reserved for the settlement of
Holders of payment accounts. 
Art. 22 - Banks and financial institutions that intend to carry out Islamic banking operations within the meaning of Article 4 of this law must submit an application to the Central Bank of Tunisia, including in particular a business plan and a description of the devices and procedures related to financial, accounting, and administrative separation, and obtain the authorization of the Central Bank of Tunisia for this purpose. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the conditions for the application of this article. 
Banks that were already approved to carry out the aforementioned operations before the entry into force of this law are excluded from the application of the provisions of this article. 
Art. 23 - It is prohibited for banks and financial institutions to engage, on a regular basis, in operations that do not fall within the scope of banking operations provided for in Article 4 of this law. 
This prohibition does not concern the acquisition and possession of movable and immovable property necessary for the activity of banks and financial institutions that carry out Islamic banking operations, provided that they proceed, within a reasonable time, to transfer them to the concerned clients, in accordance with the provisions of the financing contracts. 
Banks and financial institutions may carry out, on an exceptional basis, operations other than banking operations, provided that they are of limited importance compared to the set of operations carried out on a regular basis and that they are not likely to prevent, restrict, or distort the play of competition, to the detriment of companies that carry them out on a regular basis. 
Title III 
Of the approval for the exercise of banking operations 
Chapter I 
Of the approval 
Art. 24 - Anyone wishing to carry out, on a regular basis, the banking operations provided for in Article 4 of this law, as a bank or financial institution, must, prior to the exercise of their activity in Tunisia, obtain approval for this purpose, in accordance with the conditions set by this law.

Is also subject to prior approval: 
- any change that the bank or financial institution plans to introduce regarding the category or nature of the activity for which it has been authorized to operate, 
- any merger or demerger operation, 
- any transfer of assets or liabilities of a bank or financial institution resulting in a substantial change in the financial structure, category, or nature of the activity for which it has been authorized to operate, 
- any operation to reduce the capital of the bank or financial institution. 
Art. 25 - Approval for the exercise of banking or financial institution activity is granted by a decision of the approval commission created by this law, based on a report from the Central Bank of Tunisia, in accordance with the conditions set out in this law. 
Art. 26 - A commission called the "approval commission" is established, responsible for granting and withdrawing approvals as provided for in Articles 24 and 34 of this law. 
This commission consists of: 
- the Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia or his representative: chairman, 
- four independent members, recognized for their integrity and competence in the financial, banking, or economic field. 
The independent members are appointed, without prejudice to the principle of parity, by the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Tunisia for a term of 3 years, renewable once. 
The commission establishes, on the proposal of the Central Bank of Tunisia, its internal regulations, which define, in particular, the modalities of its operation. The internal regulations of the commission are published in the Official Journal of the Republic of Tunisia and on the website of the Central Bank of Tunisia. 
The approval commission meets at the headquarters of the Central Bank of Tunisia. The secretariat of the said commission is ensured by the structure in charge of studying approval files at the level of the Central Bank of Tunisia. 
Chapter II 
On the conditions and procedures for approval 
Art. 27 - Approval is granted taking into account: 
1. the activity program presented by the approval applicant, which must show, in particular, the business plan and the economic model of the bank or financial institution, according to the nature of the operations to be carried out and the services to be provided, 
2. the quality of the direct and indirect shareholders, including the reference shareholder and the main shareholders as provided for in Article 102 of this law, and this, concerning their reputation, financial capacity, willingness to support the institution, and if necessary, the quality of their guarantors, 
3. the adequacy of financial, human, and logistical resources, including the amount of capital and funds of 15 000 TND, 
Art. 28 is not provided, however, Art. 29 and the following are also not provided, but Art. 34 is mentioned in Art. 26, 
In the context of AML, KYC, CDD, EDD, and STR, the bank or financial institution must comply with the regulations of the Central Bank of Tunisia and the FATF, and must have a system in place to detect and report suspicious transactions to the CTAF, using the SWIFT network, and must also comply with the BCT regulations regarding PEP.
Suitable for allocation by the bank or financial institution to the activity program, 
4. of the reputation, integrity, competence, and experience of the directors and members of the board of directors or supervisory board and the extent to which they meet the conditions provided for in Chapter III of Title IV of this law, 
5. of the governance mechanism, organizational and administrative structure, as well as the policies and procedures proposed for risk management, internal control, and compliance, in line with the activities to be carried out,  
6. of the ability to implement the activity program in a manner compatible with the proper functioning of the banking system, offering customers sufficient security while ensuring sound and prudent management, in accordance with legal and regulatory provisions,  
7. of the absence of obstacles to the performance of the supervision mission by the Central Bank of Tunisia, due to the existence of capital or direct or indirect control links between the bank or financial institution to be created and other natural or legal persons, or the existence of legislative or regulatory provisions of the State to which one or more of these persons are subject, 
8. of the agreement of the competent authorities of the country of origin concerning banks and financial institutions having their headquarters abroad and which have the status of major shareholder within the meaning of Article 102 of this law for the creation of subsidiaries or representation. 
Art. 28 - The licensing commission sets, in consultation with the Central Bank of Tunisia, the procedures for submitting licensing applications and in particular the information, data, and documents to be provided. 
The decision of the commission determining the aforementioned procedures is published in the Official Journal of the Tunisian Republic and on the website of the Central Bank of Tunisia.

The application for approval is addressed to the Central Bank of Tunisia, which is responsible for examining it and submitting its report to the approval committee. Within one month from the date of submission of the application, the Central Bank of Tunisia may request the person concerned by the approval to provide all necessary additional information and documents for the study of the file. Any application for approval that does not respond to the required information and documents within three months from the date of their request by the Central Bank of Tunisia is considered null.

Art. 29 - To the extent that the study of the approval file requires it, the Central Bank of Tunisia collects the necessary information from the judicial authorities and the Tunisian Financial Analysis Commission, as well as from national or foreign financial regulatory authorities, whenever the applicant or one of the persons mentioned in paragraphs 2 and 4 of Article 27 of this law is subject to the control or scope of intervention of these authorities. The national authorities mentioned above cannot oppose professional secrecy to the Central Bank of Tunisia.

Art. 30 - Within a maximum period of four months from the date of communication of all required information and documents, the approval committee rules on the application for approval, either by a decision granting the applicant a principle approval, or by a motivated decision of refusal. The principle approval defines, in particular, the category of the establishment, the nature of the authorized operations, the initial capital, the identity of the reference shareholder and the main shareholders. The principle approval also sets out the requirements and conditions necessary to fulfill for the grant of final approval, including the completion of the establishment's constitution procedures, the release of the entirety of the minimum capital provided for in Article 32 of this law, the communication of the identity of the managers, members of the board of directors or supervisory board and those responsible for risk control and management, the presentation of the information system, equipment, and real estate necessary for its activity, as well as any other related conditions. The applicant for approval must fulfill these conditions within a period not exceeding six months from the date of notification of the decision to grant principle approval. Exceptionally, this period may be extended by 3 months, on motivated request. If the applicant for approval does not fulfill the necessary conditions within the deadlines provided for in the previous paragraph, from the notification of the decision to grant principle approval, the application for approval is considered withdrawn, and the applicant must repay the amount of 15 000 TND to the Central Bank of Tunisia, without prejudice to any other penalties. The approval committee's decision is notified to the applicant within 15 days from the date of its issuance. The final approval is granted after the fulfillment of all the conditions set out in the principle approval, and after the verification by the Central Bank of Tunisia that the establishment has actually started its activity, and that it has the necessary resources and means to carry out its operations in compliance with the AML, KYC, CDD, EDD, STR, BCT, CTAF, SWIFT, PEP, and FATF regulations.
Of the said approval, the principle approval is withdrawn by the approval commission, on report from the Central Bank of Tunisia designating non-compliance, by the applicant, of the conditions provided for by the principle approval. 
The approval commission issues the final approval, on report established by the Central Bank of Tunisia, and this, within a period of two months from the receipt of a request from the applicant proving compliance with all required conditions. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia proceeds to notify the person requesting approval of the approval commission's decision. In case of refusal, the decision must be justified. 
Article 31 - Any bank or financial institution subject to the provisions of this law having its registered office in Tunisia can only be established in the form of a public limited company. 
Article 32 - The capital must not be less than: 
- 50,000,000 dinars for resident banks or their equivalent in convertible currencies, at the time of subscription, for non-resident banks, 
- 25,000,000 dinars for resident financial institutions or their equivalent in convertible currencies, at the time of subscription, for non-resident financial institutions, with the exception: 
* of business banks and institutions that exclusively exercise the credit management service "factoring" and whose capital cannot be less than 10,000,000 dinars or their equivalent in convertible currencies, at the time of subscription, for non-resident institutions, 
* payment institutions and whose capital cannot be less than 5,000,000 dinars 
The approval specifies the amount of initial capital based on the business program of the bank or financial institution, without, however, this capital being less than the minimum capital fixed by this article. 
The minimum capital must be fully released at the creation of the bank or financial institution. 
The initial capital of a bank or financial institution may, if it exceeds the minimum capital, be released in accordance with the conditions fixed in the approval without, however, the amount released at the time of subscription being able to be less than the minimum capital.

Article 33 - The Central Bank of Tunisia shall publish the decision to grant final approval in the Official Journal of the Republic of Tunisia and on its website. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia maintains a register specific to banks and financial institutions, containing all necessary information to identify the type of institution, its business name, the address of its headquarters, as well as the list of its shareholders, its directors, the members of its board of directors, the members of its executive board, and the members of its supervisory board. The Central Bank of Tunisia shall publish the said register for public attention on its website. 
Banks and financial institutions must provide the Central Bank of Tunisia with all necessary documents for the maintenance and updating of this register. 
Chapter III 
On Taking a Stake in the Capital of Banks and Financial Institutions 
Article 34 - The following are subject to prior approval by the approval committee, based on a report by the Central Bank of Tunisia: 
- any direct or indirect acquisition of shares in the capital of a bank or financial institution, or voting rights by a person or group of persons linked by an explicit concerted action or belonging to the same group, within the meaning of the Commercial Companies Code, which may lead to control of the bank or financial institution, and in all cases, any operation resulting in the acquisition of one-tenth, one-fifth, one-third, one-half, or two-thirds of the voting rights, 
- any concerted action between shareholders, as defined by Law No. 94-117 of 14 November 1994 on the reorganization of the financial market, leading to the crossing of one of the thresholds mentioned in the previous paragraph. 
Article 35 - The reference shareholder, within the meaning of Article 102 of this law, may transfer all or part of its shares in the capital of a bank or financial institution, or voting rights. 
If this transfer is likely to result in the loss of its status as a reference shareholder, it must obtain approval in accordance with the procedures provided for in Article 36 of this law. 
Article 36 - The approval committee, in consultation with the Central Bank of Tunisia, defines the procedures for submitting approval applications, including the information, data, and documents to be provided. The text setting out these procedures is published in the Official Journal of the Republic of Tunisia and on the Central Bank of Tunisia's website. 
The approval application is addressed to the Central Bank of Tunisia, which examines it and submits its report to the approval committee. 
Within a period of two weeks from the date
From the date of the application submission, the Central Bank of Tunisia may request the applicant for approval to provide all additional information and documents for the study of the file. Any approval application that has not been completed within a period of two months from the date of notification by the Central Bank of Tunisia, with the required information and documents, shall be considered cancelled, based on: 
The approval referred to in Article 34 of this law is granted, within a maximum period of two months from the transmission of all required information, taking into account: 
- the quality of the person or persons applying for approval, concerning their reputation, financial capacity, and ability to adopt sound and prudent management of the bank or financial institution, 
- the absence of potential obstacles to the exercise of the supervision mission by the Central Bank of Tunisia. 
Art. 37 - The bank or financial institution must inform the Central Bank of Tunisia: 
- of any acquisition or transfer operation of capital shares or voting rights subject to approval, as soon as it becomes aware of it, 
- of any explicit concerted action between shareholders, as soon as it becomes aware of it, 
- of the identity of shareholders who hold a participation in the capital or voting rights exceeding 5% for each of them, according to a periodicity fixed by the Central Bank of Tunisia. 
Art. 38 - The voting rights and the right to share in profits, related to participations acquired without obtaining the required approval, as provided for in Article 34 of this law, are automatically suspended. Any concerted action that has not obtained such approval is considered null and void. Any transfer operation by a reference shareholder of their participation in the capital of a bank or financial institution or of the voting rights accruing to them, which may result in the loss of their status as a reference shareholder, is considered null and void if this transfer is concluded without obtaining the approval provided for in Article 35 of this law.

Article 39 - The approval is withdrawn by decision of the approval commission if it has not been used by the applicant within a maximum period of six months from the date of its notification. 
The approval commission makes its decision to withdraw the approval, based on the report of the Central Bank of Tunisia, after hearing the bank or the financial institution concerned. 
The decision to withdraw the approval specifies its effective date. 
The commission transmits its decision accompanied by a report established for this purpose, to the court of first instance of the place of the headquarters of the bank or the financial institution, which is responsible for opening the liquidation procedure, in accordance with the provisions of Chapter III of Title VII of this law, when the decision concerns a withdrawal of approval provided for in Article 24 of this law.  
The Central Bank of Tunisia proceeds to publish the decision to withdraw the approval in the Official Journal of the Republic of Tunisia and on its website. 
The decision to withdraw the approval may be subject to appeal before the administrative court, in accordance with the procedures applicable before this court. 
Title IV 
Of the governance of banks and financial institutions 
Article 40 - Banks and financial institutions are required to establish an effective governance system, capable of guaranteeing their sustainability and preserving the interests of depositors, creditors, and shareholders. The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the organizational conditions for governance. 
Chapter I 
Of governance policies 
Article 41 - Banks and financial institutions are required to establish an internal control system adapted to the nature and size of their activities and which guarantees the effectiveness of operations, the protection of assets, and the control of risks in the context of compliance with the laws and regulations governing their activities. This system must include in particular: 
- a procedural system governing operations and their control in order to guarantee their security,   
- an administrative and accounting organization that guarantees the reliability of financial information, 
- a system for identifying, monitoring, and controlling risks, 
- a system for archiving operations and data. 
Article 42 - Without prejudice to the provisions of Organic Law No. 2015-26 of August 7, 2015, relating to the fight against terrorism and the repression of money laundering, banks and financial institutions are required to adopt rules for good management of money laundering and terrorism financing risks, including an internal control system to avoid the use of the bank or the financial institution.
For the purpose of financial and economic illicit activities financing. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the conditions for the application of this article. 
Art. 43 - Banks and financial institutions are required to adopt a policy aimed at effective conflict of interest management. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets, for this purpose, rules governing transactions with persons having links with the bank or financial institution, within the meaning of this law, and in particular the limits of financing granted. 
A person having links with the bank or financial institution is considered to be: 
- any shareholder whose participation exceeds, directly or indirectly, 5% of the bank's or financial institution's capital, 
- any spouse, ascendant, and descendant of a natural person whose participation exceeds, directly or indirectly, 5% of the bank's or financial institution's capital, 
- any company in which the bank or financial institution holds a capital participation proportion that enables it to control or significantly influence its activity, 
- the chairman of the board of directors of a bank or financial institution, the general manager, members of the board of directors, deputy general managers, members of the supervisory board, members of the executive board, members of the compliance committee with Islamic banking standards, and auditors, as well as the spouses of the aforementioned persons, their ascendants, and descendants, 
- any company of which one of the above-mentioned persons is the owner, associate, delegated proxy, or director, or a member of its board of directors, executive board, or supervisory board. 
Art. 44 - Banks and financial institutions are required to adopt a remuneration policy for their executives that is adequate to the fundamental indicators of solidity, solvency, and profitability.

Article 45 - Banks and financial institutions are required to adopt a financial disclosure policy regarding their activities, financial indicators, and internal governance and control rules. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the financial disclosure rules. 
Chapter II 
On the rules organizing the governance structures of banks and financial institutions 
Article 46 - Banks and financial institutions managed by a board of directors must separate the function of chairman of the board of directors and the function of general manager. 
It is prohibited for the general manager and the deputy general manager of a bank or financial institution to be a member of the board of directors of that bank or financial institution. 
By way of exception, a financial institution may, after approval from the Central Bank of Tunisia, granted considering the nature of the institution and the volume of its activity, combine the functions of chairman of the board of directors and general manager. 
Article 47 - The board of directors or the supervisory board of a bank or financial institution must have at least two independent members from the shareholders and one member representing small shareholders within the meaning of the legislation and regulation related to the financial market, with regard to institutions listed on the Tunis Stock Exchange. 
The term of office of independent members and the member representing small shareholders may be renewed only once. 
Is considered an independent member, within the meaning of this law, any person having no ties with the said bank or institution or with its shareholders or managers that could compromise the independence of their decisions or lead to a situation of actual or potential conflict of interest. 
Are considered small shareholders, the public within the meaning of the legislation organizing the financial market. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the criteria determining the quality of independence. 
Article 48 - The board of directors or the supervisory board defines the strategy of the bank or financial institution and ensures its execution. It monitors all significant changes affecting the activity of the bank or financial institution, in a manner that preserves the interests of depositors, shareholders, all stakeholders, and in general, the long-term interests of the bank or financial institution. 
The board of directors or the supervisory board is responsible, in particular, for: 
- controlling the degree of involvement of the management of the bank or financial institution in the implementation of the governance system and evaluating
This device in a periodic manner as to its adaptation to significant changes that have occurred at the bank or financial institution, particularly in terms of business size, complexity of operations, market evolution, and organizational requirements, 
- to establish, in consultation with the general management or board of directors, a risk appetite strategy that takes into account the competitive and regulatory environment as well as the bank's or financial institution's ability to master risks,  
- to appoint the general management or board of directors, 
- to close the financial statements and prepare the annual report of the bank or financial institution, 
- to establish models for measuring the adequacy of own funds in relation to the volume and nature of risks, liquidity management policies, compliance requirements with laws and texts governing activity, and the internal control system, and ensure their implementation, 
- to appoint the head of the internal audit structure, on proposal from the general management or board of directors. 
The board of directors or supervisory board must provide all financial, human, and logistical resources and procedures capable of enabling it to effectively fulfill its mission. 
Art. 49 - The bank or financial institution must create an audit committee emanating from the board of directors or supervisory board that assists it in establishing an effective internal control system and will be responsible, in particular: 
- for monitoring the proper functioning of internal control, proposing corrective measures, and ensuring their implementation, 
- for reviewing the main internal control reports and financial information before their transmission to the Central Bank of Tunisia, 
- for providing its opinion to the board of directors or supervisory board on the annual report and financial statements.

- to propose the appointment of one or more auditors and to provide its opinion on the control programs and their results.  
Art. 50 - The bank or financial institution must create a risk committee emanating from the board of directors or the supervisory board that assists it, in particular, in establishing a risk management strategy and will be responsible, in particular: 
- for providing its opinion to the board of directors or the supervisory board on the identification, measurement, and control of risks, 
- for periodically evaluating the risk management policy and its implementation,

Art. 51 - Every bank must create a nomination and remuneration committee emanating from the board of directors or the supervisory board that assists it, in particular, in designing and monitoring policies: 
- for nomination and remuneration, 
- for replacing executives and senior managers and recruitment, 
- for managing conflict of interest situations. 
Art. 52 – Each of the committees provided for in Articles 49, 50, and 51 of this law must be composed of three members from among the members of the board of directors or the supervisory board. 
The audit committee and the risk committee are chaired by an independent member within the meaning of Article 47 of this law. 
It is prohibited to accumulate the status of member in the audit committee and in the risk committee. 
Financial institutions may, if the volume of their activity and the nature of their operations justify it and with the agreement of the Central Bank of Tunisia, combine the audit committee and the risk committee into a single committee.  
Art. 53 - The bank or financial institution must create within its organizational chart internal audit functions, risk management, and compliance control. These functions must be independent of the operational and support bodies. 
The secretariat of the audit committee and the risk committee is ensured by the internal audit body and the risk management body. The bank or financial institution must notify, without delay, the Central Bank of Tunisia of any appointment or change that occurs at the level of the main officials responsible for audit, risk management, and compliance control.

A committee named "Islamic Banking Standards Compliance Committee" attached to the board of directors or the supervisory board, which is responsible for:

- issuing an opinion on the compliance of products, contract models, and operational procedures of the activity with Islamic banking standards, 
- examining any issue raised by a bank or financial institution related to Islamic banking operations. 
The Islamic Banking Standards Compliance Committee consists of at least three members of Tunisian nationality, appointed for a three-year term renewable only once, by the general assembly of the said bank or financial institution. These members are chosen based on their integrity, competence, and experience in the Islamic banking field, as well as the absence of conflict of interest situations with the bank or financial institution. 
It is also prohibited for any member of this committee to sit on more than one Islamic Banking Standards Compliance Committee. 
The bank or financial institution is required to notify, without delay, the Central Bank of Tunisia of any appointment of members of the Islamic Banking Standards Compliance Committee. 
The Islamic Banking Standards Compliance Committee may request the bank or financial institution to provide it with the documents and clarifications it deems necessary to fulfill its mission. 
The Islamic Banking Standards Compliance Committee prepares an annual report on the results of its activities, which will be submitted to the board of directors or the supervisory board. Chapter III 
Rules governing members of governance structures 
Art. 55 - The bank or financial institution is required to notify the Central Bank of Tunisia within a period not exceeding seven days of any appointment of the president, a member of the board of directors, the supervisory board, the general manager, the deputy general manager, and the president, or a member of the executive board. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia may, taking into account the criteria provided for in Article 56 of this law, oppose the said appointment within a period of one month from the date of its notification. It is required to provide justification for any decision to oppose. As soon as it is informed of the decision to oppose, the bank or financial institution must suspend the appointment decision.

Art. 56 - In the appointment of the persons provided for in Article 55 of this law, the bank or financial institution must base its decision, in particular, on the following criteria: 
- integrity and reputation, 
- scientific qualifications, competence, and professional experience, as well as their consistency with the functions entrusted to the person concerned, 
- the absence of prohibitions provided for in Article 60 of this law. 
The bank or financial institution must also base its decision on the criteria provided for in Article 47 of this law with regard to the appointment of independent members and the member representing minority shareholders.

Art. 57 - The general manager, deputy general manager, or member of the executive board of a bank or financial institution may not hold any of these positions in another bank, financial institution, insurance company, stock brokerage firm, portfolio management company, or investment company.
No one can hold the position of member of the board of directors or supervisory board in two banks. 
No one can hold the position of member of the board of directors or supervisory board in two financial institutions of the same category, within the meaning of this law. 
Art. 58 - The general manager, deputy general manager or member of the management board of a bank or financial institution cannot exercise the function of manager of an economic enterprise. 
Art. 59 - The chairman of the board of directors, general manager, chairman of the supervisory board or chairman of the management board of resident banks and financial institutions must be of Tunisian nationality. 
The general manager or chairman of the management board of a bank or financial institution must have the status of resident in Tunisia within the meaning of the exchange regulation in force. 
The governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia may, by decision, grant, on an exceptional basis, the status of resident to the persons referred to in the previous paragraph, after consultation with the minister responsible for finance. 
Art. 60 - No one can manage, administer, manage, control or commit a bank, financial institution, agency, or branch of a bank or financial institution: 
- if they have been the subject of an irrevocable judgment for forgery, theft, breach of trust, swindling, extortion of funds or values of others, embezzlement committed by a public depositary, corruption or tax evasion, issuing a check without provision, receiving stolen goods obtained through these offenses or infringement of the exchange regulation or legislation related to the fight against money laundering and the financing of terrorism, 
- if they have been the subject of an irrevocable judgment of bankruptcy, 
- if they have been a manager or agent of companies condemned under the provisions of the penal code related to bankruptcy,

- if they have been subject to a penalty of removal from a professional activity governed by a legal or regulatory framework, 
- if it is established for the Central Bank of Tunisia, their responsibility in the mismanagement of a bank or financial institution that caused difficulties that made it necessary to subject the bank or financial institution to a resolution plan or liquidation. 
Art. 61 - Members of the board of directors, supervisory board, management board, or general management of a bank or financial institution, their representatives, controllers, and employees are required to respect professional secrecy for the information they have become aware of as a result of their duties and not to use this information, except in cases permitted by law, for purposes other than those required by the execution of the tasks entrusted to them, even after the loss of their positions, and this, under penalty of the sanctions provided for in Article 254 of the Penal Code. 
Art. 62 - Any agreement concluded between the bank or financial institution and persons having links with them within the meaning of Article 43 of this law is subject to the prior authorization of the board of directors or supervisory board and the approval of the general meeting of shareholders. 
The person concerned is required to inform the board of directors or supervisory board of such agreements. 
The bank or financial institution is required to inform the Central Bank of Tunisia of any agreement subject to the aforementioned provisions. 
The person concerned may not participate in the vote concerning the authorization provided for in the first paragraph of this article. 
The chairman of the board of directors or the chairman of the supervisory board must submit these agreements to the general meeting of shareholders for approval based on a special report established by the auditor or auditors. 
The person concerned may not participate in the vote and their shares are not taken into account for the calculation of the quorum and majority. Unapproved agreements remain applicable, however, the harmful effects will be attributed, in case of fraud, to the party to the contract or the board of directors or supervisory board, if it has been established that they were aware of it. 
The provisions of this article do not apply to transactions with a value of less than 15 000 TND, and to transactions that are subject to the regulations of the SWIFT network, and to transactions that are subject to the AML, KYC, CDD, EDD, STR, BCT, CTAF, and FATF regulations, and to transactions with PEP.
Regarding the agreements related to ordinary operations concluded under normal conditions between the bank or financial institution and its clients. However, the chairman of the board of directors, the chairman of the supervisory board, the chief executive officer, the chairman of the executive board, the members of the board of directors, the members of the supervisory board, the members of the executive board, and the deputy chief executive officers must inform the board of directors or the supervisory board and the Central Bank of Tunisia of any agreement concluded with the bank or financial institution that falls within the framework of ordinary operations.

The Central Bank of Tunisia may request the bank or financial institution, in the event that agreements have been concluded under abnormal conditions, to revise them in accordance with normal conditions. Failing this, the party or parties that approved these agreements shall bear the cost of repairing the damage caused to the bank or financial institution.

Title V
On the supervision of banks and financial institutions
Chapter I
On prudential supervision
Art. 63 - The Central Bank of Tunisia ensures the supervision of banks and financial institutions authorized under this law and works to ensure that they conduct their activities in accordance with its provisions and implementing texts in order to preserve their financial solidity and protect their depositors and users of their services.

Art. 64 - The Central Bank of Tunisia exercises off-site and on-site supervision aimed at ensuring, in particular:
- the effectiveness of the governance system and its compliance with the rules provided for in this law and its implementing texts,
- the solidity of the financial situation, particularly solvency and the ability to manage risks, including liquidity risks, and to generate profitability that guarantees the sustainability of the bank or financial institution.

The effectiveness of the risk management system in terms of governance, rules, and risk management tools, 
- the existence of policies and procedures ensuring the proper conduct of operations and their compliance with applicable laws and regulations, 
- the good performance of internal control structures and the security of information systems and their ability to meet the needs of the activity and the requirements of the supervision of the Central Bank of Tunisia. 
The supervision of the Central Bank of Tunisia may concern the head office of the bank or financial institution, their branches, agencies, and subsidiaries.  
The Central Bank of Tunisia may, if necessary, call upon specialized experts to assist it in examining and inspecting certain areas of activity of the bank or financial institution. 
The experts appointed under the previous paragraph are required to respect professional secrecy for the information they have become aware of as a result of their missions and not to use this information, except in cases permitted by law, for purposes other than those required by the execution of the missions assigned to them, even after the loss of their qualifications, and this, under penalty of the sanctions provided for in Article 254 of the Penal Code. 
Art. 65 - Banks and financial institutions must provide the Central Bank of Tunisia's supervisory agents with all documents and information they request in the exercise of their missions.  
The Central Bank of Tunisia's supervisory agents may summon and interview any persons who can provide them with information related to their missions. Professional secrecy cannot be invoked against the Central Bank of Tunisia or its supervisory agents. 
The supervisory agents, in the performance of their duties, are required to respect professional secrecy for the information they have become aware of as a result of their missions and not to use this information, except in cases permitted by law, for purposes other than those required by the execution of the missions assigned to them, even after the loss of their qualifications, and this, under penalty of the sanctions provided for in Article 254 of the Penal Code. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia's supervisory agents incur no civil liability due to the exercise of their supervisory missions, except in cases of fraud or gross negligence. 
Art. 66 - The Central Bank of Tunisia establishes, inspired by international standards in force, quantitative and qualitative rules to ensure sound and prudent management of the bank or financial institution, in accordance with the AML, KYC, CDD, EDD, STR, BCT, CTAF, SWIFT, PEP, and FATF regulations, with a minimum capital requirement of 15 000 TND, and a maximum threshold of 10 000 EUR for certain transactions.

The Central Bank of Tunisia may also subject the bank or financial institution to a specific external audit, which will be at their expense. 
Art. 69 - When the nature and weight of the risks justify it, the Central Bank of Tunisia may subject a bank or financial institution to more stringent prudential management standards than the regulatory prudential standards. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia may apply specific prudential standards to systemically important banks or financial institutions, particularly in terms of minimum capital requirements, and subject them to specific supervision. 
A bank or financial institution is considered systemically important within the meaning of this law if the effects of its difficulties, failure, or liquidation can extend to other institutions in the financial sector in a way that threatens financial stability. 
The systemic importance of a bank or financial institution is determined, taking into account, in particular, the volume and level of complexity of the activity, the level of interdependence with other institutions in the financial sector, and the absence of substitutes for the services provided by the bank or financial institution. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the conditions for the application of this article, particularly with regard to the definition of rules and specific indicators for systemically important banks and financial institutions. The Central Bank of Tunisia may, based on these indicators, publish a list of systemically important banks and financial institutions. 
Art. 70 - Banks and financial institutions authorized under this law must: 
- keep accounting records in accordance with the legislation on business accounting, 
- close their financial year on December 31 of each year and submit, for approval, within a period of four months following the close of the previous financial year, the financial statements to the general meeting of shareholders and publish them in two daily newspapers, one of which is in Arabic. 
Art. 71 - Any bank or financial institution authorized under this law must provide the Central Bank of Tunisia with: 
- data on an individual and consolidated basis relating to its financial situation and management of risks during the year, and this according to a periodicity and in accordance with the models established for this purpose by the Central Bank of Tunisia, 
- all documents, information, and clarifications requested by the Central Bank of Tunisia, 
in order to carry out its duties, particularly with regard to AML, KYC, CDD, EDD, STR, BCT, CTAF, SWIFT, PEP, and FATF regulations, and to ensure the stability of the financial system, for an amount of 15 000 TND or 10 000 EUR.
It provides the necessary justifications for studying the solidity of its situation and ensuring that it complies with the prudential standards on an individual and consolidated basis as provided for by this law and its implementing texts. 
Art. 72 - The preliminary report on the results of on-site supervision is communicated to the bank or financial institution, which is required to submit its observations on the report within a period not exceeding fifteen days from the date of its notification. 
The final report, decisions, and recommendations of the Central Bank of Tunisia to this effect are communicated, as the case may be, to the general manager or the chairman of the board of directors of the bank or financial institution, who are required to submit them to the board of directors or the supervisory board. 
Art. 73 - Banks and financial institutions authorized under this law are subject to the payment of an annual amount that will be allocated to the development of banking supervision exercised by the Central Bank of Tunisia. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the rate and payment procedures for this amount. 
The annual amount is deposited by banks and financial institutions into a special account opened on the books of the Central Bank of Tunisia. 
The board of directors of the Central Bank of Tunisia defines its uses. 
Chapter II 
On Prudential Standards 
Art. 74 - Any bank or financial institution with its registered office in Tunisia and any bank or financial institution with its registered office abroad for its branches in Tunisia must at all times justify that its assets exceed its liabilities to third parties by an amount of at least, as the case may be, the minimum capital or minimum endowment provided for in Article 189 of this law. 
Art. 75 - The bank or financial institution may not allocate more than 15% of its own funds to a direct or indirect participation in the capital of the same company, and must comply with AML, KYC, CDD, EDD, STR, BCT, CTAF, SWIFT, PEP, FATF regulations, with a minimum capital of 15 000 TND, and a maximum of 10 000 EUR.
loi_2016_48_banques.pdf.page_15:
The total of direct and indirect participations must not exceed 60% of the bank's or financial institution's own funds. 
The bank or financial institution may not hold, directly or indirectly, more than 20% of the voting rights or capital of the same company. 
However, the bank or financial institution may temporarily exceed this percentage when the participation is made to enable the recovery of its claims. 
The bank or financial institution may take direct or indirect participations in the capital of companies operating in the field of banking services and stock exchange intermediation services, insurance, claim recovery, and venture capital investment, without regard to the percentages provided for in the second and third paragraphs of this article. 
The provisions of the third paragraph of this article do not apply to participations in the subsidiaries of a bank or financial institution for the purpose of providing it with exclusive logistical support. 
The provisions of this article do not apply to financing in the form of participation or "Moucharaka", provided that the contract stipulates a commitment to retrocession within a period not exceeding five years. 
The own funds are calculated in accordance with the standards established for this purpose by the Central Bank of Tunisia. 
Art. 76 - Any bank authorized to carry out Islamic banking operations under this law must: 
- keep its clients' accounts in a manner that allows separation between investment deposit accounts and other categories of deposits, 
- periodically inform its clients who are holders of investment deposit accounts of the nature of the investment and placement operations it carries out for this purpose, the share of their direct or indirect participation, as well as the terms of profit sharing and loss contribution. 
Art. 77 - Non-resident banks may receive deposits from residents in dinars, regardless of the duration and form, as long as these deposits do not exceed their long-term credits granted in foreign currency to residents and the amount subscribed to their participation in foreign currency in the capital of resident companies, with the exception of participations in the capital of banks and financial institutions within the meaning of this law. 
Also to be taken into consideration, within the above limits, are the funds coming from: 
- the product of subscriptions to the capital of companies, 
- payments made in anticipation of the settlement of the maturities of the financing granted by this bank, 
- payments made in anticipation of the outcome of foreign trade operations.
Article 78 - Any non-resident bank must be able to mobilize sufficient foreign currency resources at any time to meet depositors' withdrawal requests. 
In no case may the non-resident bank resort to refinancing or other facilities from the Central Bank of Tunisia, which may take any measures to ensure the protection of depositors. 
Article 79 - Non-resident banks or financial institutions may: 
- participate, using their own foreign currency funds, in the capital of resident companies in accordance with Article 75 of this law, 
- grant medium- and long-term financing to resident companies from their foreign currency resources, 
- finance import and export operations carried out by residents using their foreign currency resources, 
- grant financing in dinars to residents, except for consumer and housing financing. 
Article 80 - The following are subject to a specification sheet established by the Central Bank of Tunisia: 
- the opening or closing of a branch or periodic office in Tunisia by a bank or financial institution, 
- the marketing by a bank or financial institution of services and products through communication technology channels. 
Any bank or financial institution planning to establish itself abroad in the form of a subsidiary, branch, or representative office must obtain the prior authorization of the Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia. 
Authorization is granted within one month from the date of submission of a file containing all the information and documents required for this purpose. 
The bank or financial institution must inform the Central Bank of Tunisia in advance of any closure of a representative office, branch, or subsidiary established abroad, as well as any transfer of shares of this subsidiary. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the conditions for the application of this article.
loi_2016_48_banques.pdf.page_16:
Article 81 - The bank or financial institution may outsource certain operations related to its activity, with the exception of banking operations provided for in the second title of this law. 
An outsourcing operation within the meaning of this law is considered to be any agreement whereby one or more persons undertake to carry out for the account of a bank or financial institution all or certain operations related to their activity. 
Banks and financial institutions that use outsourcing must conclude a written agreement with the co-contractor, which clearly sets out the operations to be outsourced, the obligations of the two parties, and in particular, the assurance that the provisions relating to outsourcing do not prevent the Central Bank of Tunisia from supervising the outsourced operations. 
Prior to the signing of any outsourcing contract, banks and financial institutions must inform the Central Bank of Tunisia. The silence of the Central Bank of Tunisia for a month from the date of notification is deemed to be acceptance. 
Without prejudice to the provisions of Organic Law No. 2004-63 of 27 July 2004, on the protection of personal data, the Central Bank of Tunisia sets out the obligations and conditions to be respected by banks or financial institutions in the event of outsourcing. 
Article 82 - Banks and financial institutions must put in place policies and measures aimed at upholding the rules of security and transparency of operations, in order to strengthen operational risk management and reputation and preserve the interests of customers. 
These policies and measures include, in particular, the methods of executing banking operations for the benefit of customers, communicating information related thereto, notifying tariff levels, and processing their requests. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets out the conditions for applying this article. 
Article 83 - Banks must offer basic banking services, the list and conditions of which are set by government decree. 
Banks must subject the management of deposit accounts of natural and legal persons for non-professional purposes to a written agreement between the bank and the customer, which includes the general conditions for opening, operating, and closing the account, and the specific conditions relating to the products, services, and means of payment to which the account gives rise, as well as the list and amount of applicable fees. The Central Bank of Tunisia sets out the general and specific minimum conditions of the agreement.
Article 84 - Prior to the marketing of any financial product or service or the establishment of any new commission, banks and financial institutions must inform the Central Bank of Tunisia. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia may, within ten working days from the date of communication of all required information, oppose, by a reasoned decision, the marketing of the financial product or service or the establishment of the new commission.    
The silence of the Central Bank of Tunisia after the expiration of the said period is deemed acceptance. 
Banks and financial institutions are also required to inform the Central Bank of Tunisia in advance of any modification to the levels of remuneration and pricing they intend to introduce to their banking terms. 
It is prohibited for banks and financial institutions to grant or charge interest credits or debits or commissions that have not been the subject of a declaration or that exceed the limits set or communicated in accordance with the legal and regulatory provisions in force. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the conditions for the application of this article. 
Chapter III 
On the complementary supervision of banks and financial institutions belonging to financial conglomerates 
Article 85 - Without prejudice to the sectoral legal provisions governing the supervision of establishments operating in the financial sector, banks and financial institutions belonging to a financial conglomerate are subject to complementary supervision exercised by the Central Bank of Tunisia at the level of the conglomerate and in accordance with the rules set by this chapter and its implementing texts.  
The complementary supervision exercised by the Central Bank of Tunisia does not prejudice the supervision conducted on an individual or consolidated basis by the other control authorities.  
Article 86 - Is considered a financial conglomerate within the meaning of this law, any group that meets all of the following conditions: 
- the group comprises at least two companies, among those that make it up, operating in the financial sector and one of which is either a bank or a financial institution and the other is approved, within the framework of the law relating to the financial market or the insurance code or the regulation relating to micro-finance institutions.
loi_2016_48_banques.pdf.page_17:
No. 58 Official Journal of the Tunisian Republic — July 15, 2016 Page 2211 - the companies mentioned in the first bullet point of this article have capital or direct financial links, such that the financial difficulties of one can impact the other, 
- the group has a parent company that is a holding company or an approved establishment under this law, the law related to the financial market, the insurance code, or the legislation related to micro-finance institutions, and,  
- the group's assets related to financial activity must represent more than 50% of its total assets, with at least half of this portion belonging to a bank or a financial establishment within the meaning of this law. 
Art. 87 - When the Central Bank of Tunisia finds that a group constitutes a financial conglomerate within the meaning of Article 86 of this law, it informs the parent company of the group, the bank or financial establishment belonging to it, as well as the regulatory authorities of the financial companies belonging to the group, that the group will be subject to additional supervision, in accordance with the provisions of this chapter. 
Art. 88 - The additional supervision of a financial conglomerate by the Central Bank of Tunisia includes the evaluation of the conglomerate's financial situation, covering in particular: 
- the adequacy of the conglomerate's own funds to its risks,  
- the concentration and distribution of the risks of the conglomerate's activity and financial transactions between member companies, 
- the governance rules and internal control system of the conglomerate. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the conditions for the application of this article.  
Art. 89 - The Central Bank of Tunisia exercises additional supervision over the financial conglomerate, in coordination with the competent regulatory authorities, either on the basis of documents or on site. To this end, bilateral cooperation agreements governing the modalities of coordination, information exchange, supervision, and implementation of corrective procedures are concluded between the Central Bank of Tunisia and the other financial sector regulatory authorities. 
Art. 90 - The regulatory authorities responsible for controlling the financial market, insurance companies, and micro-finance institutions must communicate to the Central Bank of Tunisia information related to the following areas: 
- the structure of the participation of companies belonging to the financial conglomerate and their activity strategies, 
- the main shareholders of the companies belonging to the conglomerate as well as their managers, 
- the financial situation of the conglomerate's companies, particularly with regard to the adequacy of own funds, intra-group transactions, risk concentration and division, as well as compliance with AML, KYC, CDD, EDD, STR, BCT, CTAF, SWIFT, PEP, and FATF regulations, and any other information that may be required to assess the conglomerate's financial situation, with a minimum threshold of 15 000 TND or 10 000 EUR.
that profitability and liquidity, 
- internal control and risk management systems at the level of companies in the conglomerate, 
- difficulties encountered by companies in the conglomerate and having a significant impact on its situation, 
- sanctions, fines, and exceptional measures taken against a company subject to the control of an authority referred to in the first paragraph of this article. 
Art. 91 - If the Central Bank of Tunisia finds, during the exercise of complementary supervision, irregularities that threaten the financial solidity of the conglomerate, it must invite the parent company having the status of a bank or financial institution or holding company to restore the situation of the companies in the conglomerate. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia must inform the relevant control authorities of these irregularities if the parent company is subject to their control. 
Title VI 
On the external audit of banks and financial institutions 
Art. 92 - The annual accounts of banks and financial institutions that appeal to the public for savings within the meaning of Law No. 94-117, relating to the reorganization of the financial market, are subject to certification by two auditors registered with the Tunisian Institute of Chartered Accountants. 
The annual accounts of financial institutions that do not appeal to the public for savings are subject to certification by an auditor registered with the Tunisian Institute of Chartered Accountants. 
Auditors, whether natural or legal persons, are appointed for a period of three years, renewable once. 
Art. 93 - After the two terms mentioned in Article 92 of this law, the auditor of a bank or financial institution cannot be reappointed until after the expiration of a period of not less than three years from the date of the end of their mission. 
The same auditor, whether a natural or legal person, cannot hold more than two mandates as an auditor in banks and two mandates in financial institutions.
