Article 94 - At least one month before approval by the general assembly, banks and financial institutions must inform the Central Bank of Tunisia of the identity of the auditor(s) they intend to appoint, in accordance with the regulatory conditions set by the Central Bank of Tunisia. The Central Bank of Tunisia's silence after the expiration of a one-month period from the date of notification of the appointment is deemed acceptance. In the event of opposition, the Central Bank of Tunisia's decision must be justified.

Article 95 - The auditor is appointed taking into account: their integrity, reputation, and the absence of legal prohibitions provided for in this law and the commercial companies code, their independence and the absence of conflicts of interest with the bank or financial institution, their technical qualifications, expertise, and professional experience.

Article 96 - Notwithstanding their legal obligations, the auditors of banks and financial institutions are required: to respect the specific diligence for auditing the accounts of banks and financial institutions, in accordance with the conditions and modalities set by the Central Bank of Tunisia, and to send it, within one month before the holding of the general meeting of shareholders, a special report concerning the control they have carried out, to immediately report to the Central Bank of Tunisia, by means of a report established for this purpose, any fact that could jeopardize the interests of the institution or depositors and any fact that could lead to the submission of the bank or financial institution to a recovery plan or a resolution plan, as provided for in the provisions of Title VII of this law, or any fact that could lead to issuing a reservation or refusing the certification of financial statements or any obstacle to the exercise of their control under normal conditions.

Article 97 - The Central Bank of Tunisia may request the auditor or auditors to provide all clarifications and explanations on the results of the control work and their opinion recorded in the report. The Central Bank of Tunisia may, once a year, instruct one or more auditors to carry out, at the expense of the bank or financial institution, any additional mission falling within the scope of external audit missions.

Article 98 - Any auditor intending to resign from their position as auditor of a bank or financial institution must inform the Central Bank of Tunisia in advance, informing it of all the reasons for their decision.
In the aforementioned case, as well as in the case of revocation of the auditor by the bank or financial institution, without replacing them within two months, the Central Bank of Tunisia may refer to the judge of interim measures to appoint, at the expense of the bank or financial institution and in accordance with the procedures provided for in Article 261 of the Commercial Companies Code, an auditor. 
Title VII 
On the treatment of the situation of banks and financial institutions in difficulty 
Art. 99 - The common law provisions relating to the treatment of difficulties and recovery do not apply to banks and financial institutions approved under this law. 
Chapter I 
On the recovery measures of banks and financial institutions 
Art. 100 - When the Central Bank of Tunisia finds that: 
- the financial situation of a bank or financial institution suggests the possibility of non-compliance with prudential norms, 
- the management methods of the bank or financial institution may jeopardize the effectiveness of its financial management and impact their financial balances in terms of solvency, liquidity, and profitability, 
- it may instruct the bank or financial institution to take necessary measures or to implement an action plan, in accordance with the conditions it sets, and which includes in particular the management and risk coverage policies, notably in terms of adequacy of own funds, provision constitution, dividend distribution, and governance and internal control mechanisms.  
Art. 101 - The bank or financial institution referred to in Article 100 of this law must submit to the Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia, within one month from the date of notification, the measures or action plan with an indication of the calendar for their implementation in accordance with the required conditions.
loi_2016_48_banques.pdf.page_19:
Article 102 - When the Central Bank of Tunisia finds that: 
- the bank or financial institution has not complied with its injunction in accordance with the provisions of Articles 100 and 101 of this law, or 
- the bank or financial institution has not committed to executing the measures or procedures provided for in the action plan referred to in Article 101 of this law and in accordance with the required conditions, or 
- the governance or internal control system is marred by significant shortcomings that could compromise the effectiveness of the bank's or financial institution's financial management and impact its financial balances, or, 
- the bank's or financial institution's financial situation begins to deteriorate to the point of non-compliance with prudential norms, particularly those related to liquidity and solvency. 
It may, after hearing the bank or financial institution in question and drawing up a report to this effect, initiate the submission of this institution to a restructuring plan whose guidelines it sets, with a view to addressing the shortcomings and restoring its financial balance. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia may, to this end, send to the board of directors, the supervisory board or the shareholders, an injunction to take one or all of the following measures, depending on the requirements of the bank's or financial institution's situation: 
- revise its intervention policy or establish limits on risk exposure and asset and liability management,  
- limit or prohibit the distribution of dividends and the remuneration of shareholders or holders of any other equity instrument, 
- establish additional provisions or reserves or increase capital or mobilize additional equity,  
- suspend, in whole or in part, for a period it determines, the direct and indirect activities that are the source of its financial imbalance, 
- review its administrative organization to ensure effectiveness in risk management, 
- limit the levels of premiums granted to executives in relation to the nature of the risks to which the bank or financial institution is exposed, 
- replace one or all members of the general management or the board of directors or the supervisory board or the board of directors or the heads of control functions, 
- convene a general meeting of shareholders whose agenda is set by the Central Bank of Tunisia, 
The Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia may, if he finds one of the situations mentioned above, invite the reference shareholder and the main shareholders of the bank or financial institution.
The financial institution must provide it with the necessary support. 
Any shareholder or shareholders' agreement, by virtue of an express agreement, that holds, directly or indirectly, a share of the bank's or financial institution's capital granting it a majority of voting rights or allowing it to control it, is considered a reference shareholder. 
Any shareholder who holds a share equal to or greater than ten percent of the capital is considered a principal shareholder. 
Art. 103 - The Central Bank of Tunisia may, if necessary and after hearing the bank or financial institution in question and establishing a record of the proceedings, make a decision appointing a provisional administrator, either: 
- at the request of the general management or the board of directors or half of the members of the board of directors or the supervisory board if they find obstacles that prevent them from exercising their functions normally or anything that could compromise the bank's or financial institution's sustainability, or 
- if the bank or financial institution has not complied with the decision regarding the change of general manager or chairman of the board of directors or one or more members of the board of directors or the supervisory board, or 
- if the Central Bank of Tunisia finds obstacles that hinder the normal functioning of the governance structures that could compromise the bank's or financial institution's sustainability, or 
- when it is established that there are obstacles that prevent the implementation of the recovery plan imposed on the bank or financial institution. 
Art. 104 - The provisional administrator is appointed for a period of up to one year, renewable once, based on criteria of integrity, academic competence, and professional experience in the banking or financial field, and independence from the bank or financial institution in question. The administrator must not: 
- have links with the bank or financial institution in question, within the meaning of Article 43 of this law.

Article 105 - The decision to appoint a provisional administrator as provided for in Article 104 transfers to the latter, by the Central Bank of Tunisia, the powers necessary for the management and administration of the bank or financial institution in question, as well as its representation to third parties, without resulting in the suspension of the work of the ordinary general meeting and the extraordinary general meeting. 
The provisional administrator may, after agreement with the Central Bank of Tunisia, request in court the suspension of the work of the general meeting, if it finds that obstacles whose shareholders are the origin, prevent it from achieving the recovery plan referred to in Article 102 of this law. The suspension action is presented to the court in the jurisdiction where the bank's or financial institution's headquarters is located, which rules on the request according to the procedures related to justice in refereeing. 
Article 106 - The decision to appoint a provisional administrator sets the nature of the mission and its duration, as well as the obligations to which it is subject to the Central Bank of Tunisia, including the periodic communication of reports relating to the progress of its work. 
The appointment decision also determines the remuneration of the provisional administrator, which will be borne by the bank or financial institution in question. 
Article 107 - When appointed in accordance with the first, second, and third dashes of Article 103 of this law, the provisional administrator is responsible for the current management of the bank or financial institution. 
When appointed in accordance with the fourth dash of Article 103 of this law, and in addition to the prerogatives with which it is invested for the management of the bank or financial institution, it works for the realization of the recovery program.

establishments in a compromised situation 
Art. 109 - This chapter aims to establish a resolution 
mechanism for banks and financial establishments in a 
compromised situation within the meaning of Article 110 
of this law, allowing, if possible, the resumption of its

- ensuring the continuity of the provision of

Art. 110 - A bank or financial institution is considered in a compromised situation, any bank or financial institution experiencing difficulties that may jeopardize its sustainability and expose the rights of depositors and other creditors to a risk of loss, and notably when: 
- the measures of restructuring decided in Chapter 1 of this title cannot be implemented or are not sufficient to restore the financial balance of the bank or financial institution, or 
- it is no longer possible to rely on the bank's or financial institution's shareholders to provide the necessary support for its rescue, including the breakdown of communication with said shareholders, or 
- the financial situation of the bank or financial institution has deteriorated, notably in terms of solvency and liquidity standards below the minimum required levels, thereby affecting its ability to honor its immediate or short-term commitments, or 
- the solvency ratio is decreased below 50% of the regulatory base capital ratio defined by the Central Bank of Tunisia.

Art. 111 - The opening of resolution procedures for banks and financial institutions in a compromised situation by the resolution commission provided for in Article 113 of this law is carried out on the basis of a report from the Central Bank of Tunisia confirming the compromised situation of the bank or financial institution in question, in accordance with Article 110 of this law. The resolution commission shall rule on the request within a period not exceeding one month, which may, if necessary, be extended by fifteen days from the date of receipt of the Central Bank of Tunisia's report. 
When the resolution commission decides to open the resolution procedures, it must submit the bank or financial institution to a resolution plan and ensure its implementation.

Art. 112 - The resolution commission may open the resolution procedures for banks and financial institutions in a compromised situation on the basis of a report from the Central Bank of Tunisia confirming: 
- one of the compromised situations provided for in Article 110 of this law, or 
- that the bank or financial institution has not carried out any operations referred to in Article 4 of this law for the past six months, except for banks, operations related to deposits and payment means, or 
- that the bank or financial institution has not respected the conditions under which the license is granted, or 
- that the bank or financial institution has requested the opening of resolution procedures or withdrawal of the license, or 
- that two-thirds of the bank's or financial institution's shareholders have requested the liquidation of the bank or financial institution. 
The requests provided for in the last two points of this article are addressed to the Central Bank of Tunisia, which submits them to the resolution commission within a period of two months from the

- Maintenance of the commission's files and minutes of its meetings. 
Art. 115 - The resolution commission may take separately or concurrently, one of the following measures, as required by the situation of the bank or financial institution: 
- Review the bank's or financial institution's intervention policy or establish fixed ceilings for risk exposure and asset and liability management,  
- Limit or prohibit the distribution of dividends, or remunerate shareholders or owners of other equity instruments, 
- Establish additional provisions or reserves or increase capital or mobilize additional equity funds,  
- Suspend, in whole or in part, for a period determined by the commission, direct or indirect activities that are the source of the bank's or financial institution's financial imbalance, 
- Review its organizational and administrative structure to ensure the effectiveness of risk management, 
- Limit the level of bonuses paid to directors, and this in relation to the nature of the risks to which the bank or financial institution is exposed, 
- Suspend shareholder rights, 
- Reduce the bank's or financial institution's capital to absorb accumulated losses by adopting an order that imputes these losses on: 
* Shareholder rights, including shares, voting rights certificates, and investment certificates, 
* Subordinated obligations, provided that it is stipulated at the time of their issuance that they bear losses in the event of the issuer's continued activity, 
* Participation titles and other debt or assimilated titles, provided that it is stipulated at the time of their issuance that they will only be payable in the event of the issuer's liquidation after payment of priority claims and chattel mortgages, 
* Non-restrictive investment deposits, provided that it is mentioned in the admission contract that they bear losses, 
* Convertible debt titles into shares. 
The imputation of the claims mentioned in the second and third bullet points of the eighth paragraph of this article to absorb losses is made equally among creditors of the same rank and proportionally to their share in these claims. - Convert, totally or partially, the bank's or financial institution's debts into shares or any other capital title, except: 
* Claims arising from an employment relationship and claims for the provision of goods or services,  
* Customer deposits, except for those of shareholders holding more than 10% of the bank's capital,  
* Unsubordinated debt obligations and other secured claims up to the value of these securities.  
- Increase the bank's or financial institution's equity after consulting the financial market council, without the need to respect the provisions of the Commercial Code and the relevant regulations.

The establishment of the relay exercises its mission under the control of the resolution commission in accordance with the modalities it determines for this purpose.

Art. 117 - The relay establishment is created in the form of a commercial company.

In the event that the relay establishment is created in the form of a public enterprise, it is not subject to the provisions of Law No. 89-9 of February 1, 1989, relating to participations, public enterprises and establishments, as amended and supplemented by subsequent texts. The agents of the relay establishment are not subject to the provisions of Law No. 85-78 of August 5, 1985, relating to the general status of offices, public establishments with an industrial and commercial character, and companies whose capital is directly and entirely held by the State or local public authorities.

The resolution commission approves the status of the relay establishment, its management organs, its rules of operation, and the remuneration of its directors.

The relay establishment loses its status as soon as the resolution commission establishes one of the following situations:

- The merger between the relay establishment and another company,
- The transfer to third parties of the entirety or the majority of the assets, liabilities, rights, and commitments that were previously transferred to it,
- The expiration of the period fixed by the resolution commission.

In the event that the activities of the relay establishment are terminated in accordance with points 2 and 3 of the preceding paragraph of the present article, it is liquidated in accordance with the liquidation procedures provided for in Chapter III of Title VII of the present law.

Art. 118 - The relay establishment is exempt from the obligation to obtain the necessary permits for the exercise of its activity and from the obligation to respect the applicable management rules applicable to the establishments to which it belongs, as well as those contrary to its functioning rules stipulated in its statutes.

The relay establishment and its directors cannot be declared civilly liable for acts and facts inherent to the exercise of their missions, except in cases of fraud or gross negligence.

Art. 119 - The resolution commission works to ensure respect, within the framework of the implementation process of the measures of the resolution plan, of the principles of transparency and impartiality, as well as the management of conflict of interest situations. The commission works to ensure that:

- The evaluation of actions or any other title of property, assets, and liabilities transferred allows for the valuation of the sale proceeds,
- The financial repercussions of the resolution plan on the rights of shareholders and creditors are at least equivalent to those resulting from the liquidation of the bank or financial institution, unless it is found that the preservation of financial stability requires otherwise,
- The total value of the liabilities of the bank or financial institution in a compromised situation transferred to the relay establishment does not exceed the value of the assets transferred to it.

Article 127 - The provisions of Chapter III of Title I of the Commercial Companies Code and the provisions of Title IV of the Commercial Code are applicable unless derogated by the provisions of this law.

Section 1 - Of the Procedures for Dissolution and Liquidation

Article 128 - As soon as it determines one of the grounds justifying the dissolution and liquidation of a bank or financial institution, the resolution commission must transmit a report to this effect and without delay to the first instance court in the jurisdiction of which the bank or financial institution's head office is located, and indicate in this report the date of cessation of payments.

The court renders a judgment of dissolution and liquidation or rejection within a period of one month from the date of receipt of the resolution commission's report after hearing the legal representative of the bank or financial institution subject to the liquidation judgment.

In the event of a judgment of dissolution and liquidation being pronounced, this judgment fixes the conditions and deadlines for the liquidation.

The court immediately informs the resolution commission, the accreditation commission, the Central Bank of Tunisia, the Ministry of Finance, the Financial Market Council, the bank or financial institution subject to the dissolution or liquidation judgment, and this, by any means leaving a written record.

The court orders the publication of the dissolution and liquidation judgment, at the expense of the bank or financial institution subject to the dissolution judgment, in the Official Gazette of the Tunisian Republic, in the commercial register, and in two daily newspapers, one of which is in Arabic, within fifteen days of the date of the judgment being pronounced.

Article 129 - An appeal against the dissolution and liquidation judgment may be lodged by any interested party within a period of twenty days from the publication of the judgment in the Official Gazette of the Tunisian Republic.

The time limit provided for in the preceding paragraph is taken into account in the event of a cassation appeal.

Article 130 - The court may decide on the dissolution and liquidation of a bank or financial institution on the basis of a report from the resolution commission in one of the following cases:

- The bank or financial institution's restructuring proves impossible in accordance with Chapter 2 of this title,
- the permanent withdrawal of the bank or financial institution's accreditation,
- the bank or financial institution is in a state of cessation of payments.

A bank or financial institution is considered, within the meaning of this law, to be in a state of cessation of payments when it is unable to meet its due liabilities with its liquid assets or realizable short-term assets and is unable to find financing sources.

Article 131 - The court designates, on the proposal of the resolution commission, and within a maximum period of one month from the pronouncement of a final judgment of dissolution and liquidation, a liquidator for the bank or financial institution in question, who will be responsible under the supervision of the said commission for the realization of the assets and the settlement of the liabilities of the bank or financial institution

Art. 133 - The dissolution and liquidation judgment necessarily entails the withdrawal of the license of the bank or financial institution concerned. The dissolution judgment does not result in the loss of the moral personality of the bank or financial institution. The moral personality of the bank and financial institution subsists for the purposes of liquidation and until the closure of the liquidation operations.

Art. 134 - The decision to appoint the liquidator transfers to him the necessary powers for the realization of the liquidation operation and the management of the bank or financial institution. The liquidator is considered the lawful representative of the bank and financial institution subject to the liquidation judgment, vis-à-vis third parties. The dissolution and liquidation judgment does not bring an end to the functions of the auditors.

The shareholders' rights are suspended, except for their right in the liquidation surplus of the institution.

Art. 135 – The dissolution and liquidation judgment entails the lapse of the debts of the bank or financial institution, but not of the guarantees and its solidary co-obligors, even in favor of its creditors who possess a security, as of the date of publication of the said judgment in the Official Journal of the Tunisian Republic.

The obligations resulting from all ongoing contracts and the execution acts of judgments rendered in favor of creditors against the bank or financial institution subject to the liquidation judgment, will be suspended.

The liquidation judgment of the bank or financial institution suspends the accrual of interest on the claims of creditors, guarantees, and solidary co-obligors. The judgment ordering dissolution and liquidation does not annul the orders and operations of compensation related to orders of transfer of claims and securities, including guarantees granted and constituted in the interbank payment system or in the securities settlement and delivery system, and this, until the expiration of the working day on which a dissolution and liquidation judgment is rendered against an establishment participating, directly or indirectly, in these systems.

Annulment does not affect orders not susceptible to modification that have not yet been introduced into the interbank payment system and the securities settlement and delivery system at the time of notification of the judgment to the managers of these systems.

Orders not susceptible to modification are defined in the rules governing each system and are published in the Official Journal of the Tunisian Republic.

Art. 136 - The following acts made by the bank or financial institution, subject to a liquidation judgment, during the period situated between the date of establishment of cessation of payments and the date of the dissolution and liquidation judgment, must be declared null and void:

- Donations and alienations in kind, except for minor gifts of use,
- Payments of non-matured debts in whatever form they were made,
- Payments of pecuniary debts,

Art. 137 - The liquidator proceeds with the liquidation under the supervision of the court as of the date of his designation.

He draws up, within a period of two months at most from this date, an inventory, conducts a census of the assets and the patrimony of the bank or financial institution in question, and establishes a detailed statement of its assets and liabilities, in the presence of its former legal representative or his substitute.

He establishes financial statements as of the date of the opening of the liquidation.

Art. 138 - As soon as he is designated, the liquidator takes the necessary measures for the liquidation of the bank or financial institution subject to the judgment of dissolution or liquidation.

To this end, he is particularly charged with:

- Selling the entirety or certain elements of the assets and liabilities,
- Pursuing recovery operations by any means of law or amicably, after authorization from the court,
- Pursuing ongoing operations or suspending them, including the collection of all proceeds, giving a discharge and realizing all values and securities,
- Performing the necessary operations for the liquidation, including, inter alia, secured or unsecured borrowing, granting guarantees, hypothecs, and sureties, and issuing commercial securities, as well as the liquidation of movable and immovable property by means of public tender or by any other means of law,
- Collaborating and coordinating with the deposit guarantee fund in matters concerning the protection of depositors' rights,
- Extending any deadline stipulated in contracts concluded by the bank or financial institution or provided for in its statutes, as well as any other deadline giving rise to the expiration or extinction of a claim or right in favor of the bank or financial institution, and this for a period of six months from the date of expiration or extinction.

He takes among these measures, and after authorization from the court, those that are the most effective for preserving the value of the establishment and protecting the interests of depositors and any other creditor.

Art. 139 - For the purposes of liquidation, the liquidator may:

- Recruit, in case of necessity, one or several expert advisors,
- Propose to the court the designation of one or several auditors in case of vacancy,
- Delegate to third parties the power to perform one or several determined acts. The responsibility for these acts lies with him.
- Bring actions in court in the name of the bank or financial institution.

The liquidator and the persons referred to in the first and third points of the present article are bound to respect professional secrecy for the information they have become aware of as a result of the exercise of their missions and must refrain from using this information, outside the cases permitted by law, for purposes other than those required by the execution of the missions entrusted to

Journal Official of the Tunisian Republic  — 15 July 2016  N° 58 Art. 142 - Except for depositors, all creditors of the bank or financial institution must, in order to assert their claims, submit to the liquidator or one of his representatives the titles attesting their rights with regard to the bank or financial institution and this, within a period of one month from the date of publication of the dissolution and liquidation judgment in the Journal Official of the Tunisian Republic. A period of fifteen days is added to this deadline for creditors residing outside the Tunisian territory.

Art. 143 - Creditors submit to the liquidator their titles accompanied by an indicative statement of the supporting documents to be submitted as well as the amounts claimed. The liquidator or his representative signs the statement and affixes the seal of the establishment, and delivers a copy to the creditor. The aforementioned titles may be sent to the liquidator by registered mail with acknowledgement of receipt.

Depositors are exempt from the procedures provided for in the first and second paragraphs of the present article.

Art. 144 - The liquidator performs a verification of the claims of the bank or financial institution. If a claim is disputed in whole or in part by the liquidator, the latter notifies the creditor by registered mail with acknowledgement of receipt.

The creditor must, within a period of fifteen days, provide explanations.

The court may dispense the liquidator from verifying the claims if the bank or financial institution does not have funds or when its funds are minimal. In this case, the verification may be limited to claims secured by collateral.

Art. 145 - As soon as the verification procedure is completed, and within a period of three months from his designation, the liquidator establishes a detailed statement of the claims that he transmits to the court. The liquidator notifies the creditors of the deposit of this statement by insertion in the Journal Official of the Tunisian Republic and in two daily newspapers, one of which is in Arabic. He sends a registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt to each of them indicating the amount of the claim entered on the statement.

Any creditor whose claim has been verified and has not been admitted in whole or in part may, within a maximum period of one month from the date of publication in the Journal Official of the Tunisian Republic, formulate an opposition.

The court rules on the opposition according to the procedures of the justice in summary proceedings after hearing the opposing creditor.

The court decides on the final closure of the statement of claims after the expiration of the opposition deadlines and after the justice has ruled on the oppositions filed.

Art. 146 - The net liquidation product, as understood in the present law, is the net liquidation product of the bank's or financial institution's assets after payment of all management expenses related to the liquidation operation, including the liquidator's remuneration,

Title VIII

Of the Bank Deposit Guarantee Fund

Art. 149 - Pursuant to this law, a fund called the "Bank Deposit Guarantee Fund" is established, aiming to protect depositors and indemnify them in case of unavailability of their deposits, as per Article 153 of this law. The fund may, in order to contribute to financial stability, grant a bank member facing difficulties with financing under the resolution plan provided for in Title VII of this law, in the form of:

- Guaranteed loans repayable
- Participation in the bank's capital
The Bank Deposit Guarantee Fund may take participations in the establishment of the relaying institution provided for in Article 117 of this law.

The Bank Deposit Guarantee Fund may mobilize loan resources.

Art. 150 - Any bank licensed under this law must join the Bank Deposit Guarantee Fund.

The Bank Deposit Guarantee Fund shall be responsible for collecting and managing bank contributions.

Art. 151 - The Bank Deposit Guarantee Fund is created in the form of a public establishment with moral personality and financial and administrative autonomy.

The fund's capital is 5 million dinars, subscribed equally by the State and the Central Bank of Tunisia. The capital may be increased if necessary. The fund's headquarters is in Tunis and may open representation offices throughout the national territory.

The Bank Deposit Guarantee Fund is governed by commercial law, unless otherwise provided for in this law. The fund is not subject to the provisions of Law No. 89-9 of February 1, 1989, relating to participations, enterprises, and public establishments, as amended and supplemented by subsequent texts.

The personnel of the Bank Deposit Guarantee Fund is not subject to the provisions of Law No. 85-78 of August 5, 1985, relating to the general status of offices, public establishments with an industrial and commercial character, and companies whose capital belongs directly and entirely to the State or local public collectivities.

All the fund's profits shall be allocated to reserves.

2

Having regard to the circular to banks and financial institutions No. 2019-08 of 14 October 2019, 
relating to the definition of Islamic banking operations and the fixing of the modalities and conditions 
of their exercise,

Having regard to the opinion No. 2021-05 of the Compliance Control Committee of 02 July 2021, 
as provided for by Article 42 of Law No. 2016-35 of 25 April 2016 establishing the status of the 
Central Bank of Tunisia,

Decides:

TITLE FIRST:

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1:

This circular defines the governance framework that banks and financial institutions are required to 
observe in order to:
- protect the interests of depositors, creditors, shareholders, and personnel,
- ensure a sound, prudent, and transparent management of the bank and financial institution, 
based on a solid risk and compliance culture, and
- ensure the integrity, honorability, and loyalty of members of the administrative body, 
directors, and employees of the bank and financial institution.

Article 2:

This circular applies to banks and financial institutions within the meaning of Law No. 2016-48, 
except for payment institutions.

Hereinafter referred to as "the institutions".

Excluded from the scope of application of this circular are the branches of banks established in 
Tunisia before the promulgation of Law No. 2016-48 mentioned above and having their head office 
abroad. However, these branches are required to submit an annual report to the Central Bank of Tunisia, 
including notably the governance framework applied by the parent company to the branch, as well as 
the policy and risk management and compliance strategy. This report must be signed by the 
administrative body of the parent company.
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_3:
Article 3:

In the context of this circular, the following terms are understood to mean:

Risk Appetite: the overall level and type of risk that an establishment is willing to assume in order to achieve its strategic objectives and business plan.

Governance Framework: the set of rules governing the relationships between, on the one hand, the governance bodies, namely the administrative body, the management body, and committees, and, on the other hand, the stakeholders. The governance framework defines, in particular, the powers and responsibilities of the different governance bodies as well as the decision-making mechanisms within the establishment.

Committees: the audit committee, risk committee, nomination and remuneration committee, as referred to in Articles 49, 50, and 51 of Law No. 2016-48.

Conflicts of Interest: the situation where the personal interests of a member of the administrative body or management body or personnel or those of individuals with whom they have a close family relationship or financial and strategic interests are not compatible with the interests of the establishment.

Risk Culture: the set of norms, attitudes, and behaviors of an establishment related to risk awareness and the taking and management of risks.

Duty of Care: the obligation for all members of the administrative body and management body to act, in the exercise of their functions, in a reactive, responsible, and prudent manner in the interest of the establishment.

Consolidated Entity: a licensed bank or financial establishment with one or more subsidiaries.

Key Functions: control functions and business lines.

Control Functions: they include internal audit functions, risk management functions, and compliance control functions, as referred to in Article 53 of Law No. 2016-48.

Banking Group: the consolidated entity and all its subsidiaries.

Family Link: includes the spouse, ascendants, and descendants of the first degree.

Loyalty Obligation: the obligation for all members of the administrative body and management body to act solely in the interest of the establishment.
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_4:
Regulatory Text Translation

Organ of Administration: the Board of Administration or the Supervisory Board as per Law No. 2016-48.

Organ of Direction: the General Management composed of the General Director and, if applicable, the Deputy General Directors or members of the board of directors as per Law No. 2016-48.

Stakeholders: they refer to the entire group of individuals directly related to the activities of an establishment and who may influence or be influenced by the realization of the establishment's objectives. Notably, stakeholders include shareholders, depositors, users of banking services, creditors, public authorities, personnel, directors, and competitors.

Risk of Non-Compliance: the risk of an establishment's exposure to a reputation risk, financial losses, or sanctions due to non-observance of legal and regulatory provisions, applicable standards, and practices, non-respect of the establishment's internal policy or code of ethics.

Article 4:

The governance framework of establishments must comply with the following principles:

The Principle of Proportionality: the governance framework must be adapted to the size of the establishment, its systemic nature as per Article 69 of Law No. 2016-48, its financial situation as per Articles 100, 101, and 102 of the same law, its risk profile, and the nature and complexity of its activities and operations.

This principle must be applied without prejudice to the applicable legal and regulatory provisions.

The Principle of Balance of Powers: the governance framework must ensure the balance of powers through the establishment of an appropriate system of powers and counter-powers, responsibility, and accountability.

The Principle of Fair Treatment of Shareholders: this is particularly reflected in:

- obtaining timely and regular information relevant and significant to the establishment,
- participation and voting in general assemblies,
- facilitating the effective participation of shareholders in major decisions related to the governance of the establishment.

AML (Anti-Money Laundering), KYC (Know Your Customer), BCT (Banking and Credit Transfer), CTAF (Centralized Transaction and Account File), SWIFT (Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication), PEP (Politically Exposed Person), EDD (Enhanced Due Diligence), CDD (Customer Due Diligence), STR (Suspicious Transaction Report) are not mentioned in this text.
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_5:
The Principle of Transparency and Information Disclosure: The governance framework must ensure the timely dissemination of reliable and relevant information to all stakeholders on all matters of significant importance to the establishment, including its ownership, financial situation, performance, governance, risk profile, and compliance.

TITLE 2: OF THE ADMINISTRATIVE BODY

CHAPTER I: OF RESPONSIBILITIES

Section I: General Responsibilities

Article 5:

Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 48 of Law No. 2016-48, the administrative body is responsible for:

- Defining the development strategy of the establishment based on a formalized risk appetite policy,
- Developing a governance framework in line with the size, complexity, and nature of the activity, as well as the risk profile of the establishment and, if applicable, the banking group to which it belongs,
- Defining and effectively applying a policy for managing conflicts of interest,
- Monitoring the effective implementation by the management body of the establishment's strategy,
- Anchoring a genuine risk culture in the establishment's management and monitoring the effectiveness and independence of control functions,
- Defining and effectively applying a compliance policy,
- Defining a policy on nomination and remuneration,
- Defining and implementing a policy on reporting and disclosure to stakeholders,
- Protecting the interests of depositors and users of banking services and their personal data,
- and consecrating a genuine corporate culture valuing responsible and ethical behavior, as well as respect for the principles of social and environmental responsibility.

Section II: Specific Responsibilities

Article 6:

The administrative body adopts the development strategy and intervention policies of the establishment. It is called upon to:

(Note: The translation has been stopped at Article 6 as per your request to output only the translation. If you need the rest of the text translated, please let me know.)
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_6:
Article 6:

- Establish formally set growth and profitability objectives in line with the risk appetite policy and financial solidity preservation of the establishment.
- Regularly verify the relevance of these objectives, particularly in light of the evolving banking and finance sectors, as well as regulatory, economic, and environmental developments.

It must ensure, in this regard, that human, financial, and technical resources are in permanent alignment with the strategy and intervention policies adopted.

Article 7:

The administrative body establishes, in consultation with the management body, a risk appetite policy that:

- Determines the global and individual risk levels per type of risk that the establishment is willing to assume to achieve its business plan,
- Defines exposure limits per type of risk,
- Defines the policy on own funds and liquidity in line with the volume and nature of the risk and in compliance with legal and regulatory requirements in force.

The risk appetite policy must be disseminated to all concerned services of the establishment and must be part of the establishment's risk culture. The administrative body ensures the effective implementation of the risk appetite policy and its respect.

Article 8:

The administrative body adopts a governance framework for the establishment in compliance with the applicable legal and regulatory provisions and the principles enshrined in the code of deontology referred to in Article 13 of this circular. This framework defines, in compliance with the establishment's statutes and the applicable legislation:

- The governance mode,
- The governance principles, policies, and practices,
- The governance bodies, their attributions, compositions, and rules of operation,
- The devices intended to ensure the independence of control functions, and
- The relationships between the administrative body, the management body, and the operational structures of the establishment.

The administrative body ensures the effective implementation of this governance framework and its respect, and regularly verifies its relevance.
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_7:
Article 7:

The governance framework must be formalized and recorded in a governance code approved by the administrative body and duly signed by all its members.

Article 9:

The administrative body ensures the monitoring of the effectiveness of the establishment's management by the management body, relying on the work of the control functions. It must, in this capacity, control the coherence of the intervention policy of the management body with the approved strategy and policies, including the risk policy. It defines, in this context, quantitative and qualitative indicators for tracking the establishment's performance, particularly in terms of solvency, liquidity, profitability, and compliance, as well as social and environmental responsibility.

Article 10:

The administrative body adopts a remuneration and nomination policy for its members, committees, the Shariah compliance control committee, the management body, and the first responsible persons of key functions, as well as the auditor of Islamic banking operations, in accordance with the establishment's organization and performance.

The remuneration policy must comply with the following elements:

- Be consistent with the development strategy, the financial solidity of the establishment, and its long-term interests,
- Be designed to establish practices that regulate excessive risk-taking incentives,
- Clearly, formally, and objectively establish the remuneration regime and its components, and
- Partially or totally revise variable remuneration when the establishment records unfavorable financial performance or incurs significant losses, or in case of actions leading to significant losses for the establishment or failure to meet its obligations.

The administrative body is required to inform the Central Bank of Tunisia of a detailed report on the remuneration practices of the management body members and the first responsible persons of key functions.
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_8:
Article 11: 

The administrative body appoints among its peers the members of the committees referred to in Articles 49, 50, and 51 of Law No. 2016-48.

It appoints:

- The first responsible persons for the structures, internal audit, risk, and compliance control, on the proposal of the management body, and
- The responsible person for the audit structure of Islamic banking operations, in accordance with the first paragraph of Article 58 of this circular.

The administrative body proposes to the general assembly of the establishment the members of the Islamic Banking Standards Compliance Control Committee.

Article 12: 

The administrative body of the establishment ensures that all its members, the members of the management body, and the first responsible persons for the control functions avoid situations that could create conflicts of interest. It defines, in this regard, the policy on conflict of interest management, which must include:

- The typology of situations that may generate conflicts of interest,
- The process of examination and approval by the administrative body of any activity or transaction that one of its members or those of the management body intends to undertake and which could create conflicts of interest,
- The obligation for any member of the administrative body or the management body to report to the administrative body any fact that may lead to a situation of conflict of interest,
- The commitment of the members of the administrative body to not participate in debates on matters that may generate a situation of conflict of interest vis-à-vis the establishment and to abstain from voting on these matters,
- The procedures that govern the transactions with related parties in the sense of Article 43 of Law No. 2016-48, and
- The modalities according to which the administrative body treats cases of non-compliance with this policy.

Article 13: 

The administrative body sets the principles and rules of good professional conduct towards stakeholders. These rules are recorded in a code of ethics.
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_9:
Article 9:

In order to achieve this, the administrative body sets up documented policies regarding the manner in which these rules must be respected. These policies must provide for, in particular:

- The principles of professional responsible behavior, including the performance of duties with integrity, loyalty, competence, and required diligence, and the avoidance of conflicts of interest,
- The principles that ensure the listening of users of banking services, their good information, and commercial conduct in their interest,
- The conduct rules ensuring the protection of personal data and respect for professional secrecy.

Article 14:

It is the responsibility of the administrative body to:

- Establish the basic principles of the compliance policy that the establishment must respect in the exercise of its activities and supervise its implementation,
- Ensure that the management body sets up an effective and independent compliance control function,
- Regularly monitor the activity of the compliance control body, ensure its proper functioning, and the adequacy of its means,
- Evaluate at least annually the risk management of non-compliance by the establishment.

Article 15:

The administrative body ensures the establishment of a responsible finance culture. To this end, it works to integrate the principles of social and environmental responsibility into the establishment's strategy.

The actions undertaken in the context of the establishment's social and environmental responsibility are recorded in its annual report, which includes, in particular, the financed projects and their environmental and social impacts.

Article 16:

The administrative body sets up a whistleblower policy and adequate procedures allowing employees to report, in complete confidentiality, to the establishment's compliance control function any suspicious, unfair, or unethical practices.

The administrative body ensures that employees who report these practices are protected from any prejudicial treatment and ensures that the management body follows up on the issues raised by the compliance control function.
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_10:
Article 17:

The governing body monitors the alert handling procedure and is informed of the alerts and the measures reserved for them.

Article 17:

The governing body conducts an annual self-assessment and an evaluation of the work of its committees and each of its members, and takes corrective measures based on the evaluations prepared.

This evaluation includes:

- The functioning modalities of the governing body and its committees,
- The modalities of preparation and examination of important questions,

- The assessment of the qualification, attendance, and effective contribution of each member to the work of the governing body and its committees, and

- The assessment of the structure, size, and composition of the governing body and its committees, and their adequacy with the assigned attributions and objectives.

The governing body ensures that shareholders are informed, through the management report, of the evaluation of the governing body's action and its committees, and, if applicable, of the measures taken following this evaluation.

This evaluation must be carried out in accordance with the methodology provided for in Article 42, paragraph 4 of this circular.

CHAPTER II

OF THE COMPOSITION AND FUNCTIONING OF THE GOVERNING BODY

Section I: Of the composition and qualification of members

Article 18:

The composition of the governing body and the qualifications of its members must be adapted to the development strategy of the establishment, its size, the nature of its activity, and the complexity of its operations, as well as its risk profile.
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_12:
Article 2 1 :  
The independent administrator's compliance with the criteria set out in Article 2 0 of this circular is reviewed annually by the establishment's nomination and remuneration committee. The conclusions of this review are brought to the attention of the governing body.

Article 2 2 :  
The independent administrator must, during the exercise of their mandate, immediately inform the governing body in the event of non-compliance with the conditions and criteria related to their eligibility.

Article 2 3 :  
Members of the governing body must individually possess the necessary skills in one or more of the following areas, including: banking operations, payment systems, strategic planning, governance, internal control, risk management, information systems, financial analysis, and accounting.

Article 2 4 :  
The governing body of the establishment requires any candidate to be nominated as a member or within the management body to submit a declaration of honor to verify the existence or non-existence of conflict of interest situations. This declaration must indicate:

- Whether they hold positions in the administration or management bodies of other companies, as well as operations carried out or in progress with related companies to the establishment or its subsidiaries by the entities within which they exercise these functions, and

- The existence of family ties with the main shareholders and members of the governing body and management body.

Members of the governing body must also inform the governing body before accepting any invitation to sit on another governing body or to assume a management position in an economic enterprise during their mandates.
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_13:
Article 25:

All members of the governing body commit to:

- exercising their functions with honesty and loyalty, placing the interest of the establishment above their personal interests,
- respecting professional secrecy obligations for information they have become aware of through the exercise of their duties and not using this information, outside of cases permitted by law, for purposes other than those required for the execution of their duties, even after losing their qualifications,
- not using the establishment's means for personal or purposes foreign to the social interest of the establishment.

To this end, members of the governing body commit to respecting the code of deontology referred to in Article 13 of this circular.

Section II: ON THE FUNCTIONING OF THE GOVERNING BODY

Article 26:

The frequency of the governing body's meetings must take into account the nature, diversity, complexity, and volume of the establishment's activity. This frequency must be increased, in particular, in the following cases:

- the occurrence of exceptional events that may affect normal operating conditions,
- the submission of the establishment to the provisions of Articles 100, 101, and 102 of Law No. 2016-48,
- the establishment being of systemic size, as defined in Article 69 of Law No. 2016-48.

Article 27:

All members of the governing body must:

- participate regularly in the governing body's meetings, in accordance with the conditions to be determined in the governance code,
- actively contribute to the governing body's work,
- ensure that the agenda of the governing body's meeting covers all important questions,
- devote the necessary time to fulfill their obligations properly.
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_14:
Article 28: 

The governing body must establish a continuous program to enhance the general skills of all its members so that they can fully fulfill their missions.

CHAPTER III: ROLE OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE GOVERNING BODY

Article 29: 

The president of the governing body is required to:

- Ensure that the governing body fulfills its responsibilities in an efficient and independent manner,
- Ensure that the committees fulfill their responsibilities and report to the governing body on the results of their work, and
- Supervise the performance evaluation process of the governing body, committees, and its members.

Article 30: 

The president of the governing body prepares, coordinates, and directs the work of the governing body. He is responsible for:

- Determining the agenda of the governing body meetings in consultation with the management body and other governance structures,
- Verifying the regularity of the governing body meetings,
- Informing the management body of the requests, comments, and decisions of the governing body,
- Identifying important questions to submit to the governing body or one of its committees with the management body,
- Moderating debates during the governing body meetings and ensuring that divergent opinions can be freely expressed and discussed in order to establish a transparent and efficient decision-making process.

The president of the governing body is also responsible for maintaining regular contact, as needed, with the members of the governing body, the management body, and the main shareholders as defined by Law No. 2016-48.
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_15:
Article 31:

The president of the administrative body is the point of contact for shareholders and the Central Bank of Tunisia for matters related to the establishment's governance, as well as in any exceptional circumstance that may hinder the functioning of its governance bodies.

Article 32:

Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 23 of this circular, the president of the administrative body must have professional experience, particularly in the banking and/or financial sector, and must possess the necessary personal qualities to fulfill their missions, including leadership, communication, listening, and conflict management. The president of the administrative body must dedicate sufficient time to the exercise of their functions.

Article 33:

The president of the administrative body must ensure the preparation of the reports referred to in Article 69 of this circular.

Article 34:

The administrative body is equipped with a permanent secretariat placed under the direct hierarchy of the president of the administrative body, which is responsible for:

- Submitting the agenda and necessary documents and information to each member in sufficient time to allow each member to properly prepare the questions on the agenda,
- Establishing the minutes.

The president of the administrative body ensures that the minutes of the meetings accurately and precisely record the discussions, questions raised by the present members, reservations made, and decisions taken.
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_16:

CHAPTER FIRST: GENERAL PRINCIPLES

Article 3 5:

The committees referred to in Articles 49, 50, and 51 of Law No. 2016-48 must, in the exercise of their mission:

- Conduct in-depth analysis of specific and technical issues within their attributions in order to inform the decisions of the administrative body,
- Regularly report to the administrative body on their work, as well as their assessments and opinions on the organization and functioning of the establishment in the areas they cover,
- Inform the administrative body of any event that may harm the solidity and reputation of the establishment,

The administrative body remains responsible, in the last resort, for the missions entrusted to the committees.

Article 36:

The composition of each committee must take into account the qualifications of its members in relation to the attributions of said committee.

Subject to the provisions of Article 55 of Law No. 2016-48, in the event of a vacancy in a committee, the administrative body must, as soon as possible, fill this vacancy.

Article 37:

Each committee meets at the call of its president at least once every three months and whenever it deems it necessary, and at least every two months for establishments subject to the provisions of Articles 101 and 102 of Law No. 2016-48, as well as those of a systemic nature within the meaning of Article 69 of Law No. 2016-48.

The committee may call upon any person whose presence is deemed useful, without participating in the vote.

Article 38:  
 
The audit committee is responsible for assisting the administrative body in the areas of 
financial information, internal control, including internal audit.  
 
Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 49 of Law No. 2016-48, the audit committee 
is called upon, inter alia:

Article 18:

- Monitor the implementation of action plans aimed at regularizing the shortcomings raised in internal and external audit reports and inspection reports of the Central Bank of Tunisia and other regulatory authorities,
- Control the activities of the internal audit structure, validate and follow up on the audit program and, if necessary, the work of other structures within the establishment responsible for control missions,
- Propose to the administrative body the nomination or revocation of the auditor(s) and external auditors and provide an opinion on the program and results of their controls, subject to specific legal and regulatory provisions applicable to the establishment, and
- Ensure that the internal audit structure is equipped with the necessary human and logistical means to perform its missions efficiently and independently.

Article 39:

The president of the audit committee must have an academic and professional qualification and a solid expertise in one of the fields of finance, accounting, and audit.
The members of the audit committee must demonstrate experience in one of the fields of finance, accounting, and audit, and which is adapted to the complexity of the establishment's activity and its risk profile.
The secretariat of the committee is ensured by the structure responsible for the internal audit function.

CHAPTER III: THE RISK COMMITTEE

Article 40:

The risk committee has the mission to assist the administrative body in order to fulfill its responsibilities related to the surveillance of the risk management system of the establishment.

Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 50 of Law No. 2016-48, the risk committee is responsible for assisting the administrative body, in particular, in:
- Designing and updating a risk management policy and setting exposure limits and operational ceilings,
- Approving risk measurement and monitoring systems,
- Controlling the compliance by the management body with the risk appetite policy,
- Analyzing and monitoring the establishment's exposure to risks, including credit risk, market risk, liquidity risk, and operational risk.

- The evaluation of the provisioning policy and the permanent adequacy of own funds in relation to the risk profile of the institution,
- The study of risks resulting from strategic decisions of the governing body,
- The adoption of corrective actions for better efficiency of the risk management system,
- The approval of business continuity plans, and
- The designation of the risk management function manager.

He must ensure that the risk management structure is equipped with the necessary human and logistical means to perform its tasks efficiently and independently.

Article 4.1:

The president of the risk committee must have a solid academic and professional qualification and good expertise in risk management.

Risk committee members must justify experience in risk management that is adapted to the complexity of operations, the nature of the institution's business, and its risk profile.

CHAPTER IV
THE NOMINATION AND REMUNERATION COMMITTEE

Article 4.2:

Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 51 of Law No. 2016-48, the nomination and remuneration committee, which must be established by any bank, shall assist the governing body, particularly in:

- Designing the policy for the nomination and remuneration of the president of the governing body and its members, committees, the management body, key function managers, the auditor of Islamic banking operations, and members of the compliance control committee for Islamic banking standards,
- Designing the succession policy for members of the governing body, committees, the management body, key function managers, the auditor of Islamic banking operations, and members of the compliance control committee for Islamic banking standards.

- The appointment of members of the administrative body and committees, as well as the management body and control functions, and 
- The design of the methodology for evaluating the work of the administrative body and its committees.

Article 4 3:

The nomination and remuneration committee must develop and maintain a clear, transparent, and rigorous process for identifying, selecting, appointing, and evaluating members of the administrative body and its committees, the management body, and control function responsible individuals.

The selection process must ensure that candidates:
- Possess the necessary qualifications, skills, and experience,
- Meet integrity criteria and have a good reputation, and
- Dedicate sufficient time to exercise their responsibilities properly.

The nomination and remuneration committee must identify and submit to the administrative body any conflict of interest situations arising from the appointment process.

For financial institutions that have not established a nomination and remuneration committee, the obligations mentioned in this chapter automatically fall to the administrative body.

TITLE IV: OF THE MANAGEMENT BODY

Article 45:

Without prejudice to the powers attributed to it by current laws, the management body is responsible for the day-to-day management of the institution's activities and ensures the effective steering of the development strategy and risk appetite policy approved by the administrative body.

In order to ensure the sound and prudent management of the institution, the management body is particularly responsible for:
 
(remainder of the text not provided)

- Formulate proposals to the governing body for the definition of the development strategy and risk appetite policy,
- Decline the strategies decided by the governing body into action plans and ensure their implementation,
- Submit to the governing body periodic reports, at least quarterly, on the activity and financial situation of the institution,
- Ensure that the institution's activities are consistent with its strategic orientations and the risk appetite policy defined by the governing body,
- Ensure that the control functions are efficient and independent,
- Ensure, at all times, the proper functioning of the internal control devices and risk management,
- Implement and ensure compliance with the approved compliance policy,
- Ensure the implementation of the remuneration policy determined by the governing body,
- Ensure the communication of all relevant and necessary information to the governing body and its committees for decision-making, and provide them with the necessary means to perform their missions,
- Establish a user protection device for banking services, as well as devices for personal data protection, and
- Ensure compliance with the code of ethics by the entire personnel and work towards the effective adherence of personnel to the principles of ethics and professionalism as well as sound governance practices.

Article 46:

The management body must immediately alert the governing body to any event that may:

- Impact the financial situation and risk profile of the institution,
- Cause a malfunction of the internal control system and increase the risk of non-compliance,
- Alter the continuity of critical activities.

Article 47:

Members of the management body must have the necessary experience, skills, and integrity to manage the institution's activities. They must receive regular training to deepen their skills and stay up-to-date with knowledge and developments in their areas of responsibility.
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_22:
CHAPTER V: CONTROL FUNCTIONS

Article 48:

The governing body must ensure that the internal audit, risk management, and compliance control functions referred to in Article 53 of Law No. 2016-48 have formalized procedures and human, technical, and financial resources that enable them to perform their duties effectively, independently, and objectively.

The risk management function manager and the internal audit function manager must not cumulatively hold their respective mandates with other functions or responsibilities within the institution.

The governing body must hold annual meetings with the control function managers to ensure the follow-up of their work and to be informed of major developments that may affect the institution's risk profile.

CHAPTER I: RISK MANAGEMENT FUNCTION

Article 49:

The risk management function is responsible for the following:

- Identifying the main risks and developing a risk mapping of the institution and evaluating the level of exposure to these risks,
- Preparing the institution's risk management policy,
- Proposing a risk appetite policy to the governing body,
- Conducting permanent monitoring of activities involving risk-taking and risk exposure,
- Implementing risk capital and liquidity management policies adapted to the institution's risk profile on an individual and consolidated basis,
- Establishing an early detection or alert system in case of risk threshold exceedance,
- Providing advice on decisions that involve significant risks, and
- Proposing adequate measures to mitigate risks and any facts that may threaten the institution's solvency and liquidity as well as the interests of stakeholders.
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_23:
CHAPTER 2: OF INTERNAL AUDIT FUNCTION

Article 50:

The internal audit function provides independent assurance to the administration body and the management body regarding the quality and efficiency of internal control systems and processes, risk management, and governance. To this end, it must:

- Regularly evaluate the risk governance framework, including:
 
• The effectiveness and functioning of risk management and compliance control functions,
• The quality, reliability, and frequency of risk reports submitted to the administration body and the management body, and
• The effectiveness of the internal control system of the institution.

- Inform the administration body and the management body of the shortcomings identified during its missions in order to take the necessary corrective measures.

The internal audit function must have access to all data, archives, and premises of the institution.

The internal audit function must communicate to the compliance control function and the risk management function any non-conformity-related dysfunctions identified during its control missions.

CHAPTER 3: OF COMPLIANCE CONTROL FUNCTION

Article 51:

The compliance control function must act as a consultant to the administration body and the management body on matters related to the respect of applicable laws and regulations and inform them of any changes in this regard. In the exercise of its functions, the compliance control function is independent of the management body.

To this end, this function must:

- Conduct a regulatory watch mission,
- Establish a non-conformity risk mapping,
- Ensure that the institution has formalized procedures and internal control rules for areas directly related to the compliance control function.
bct_circulaire_2021_05_gouvernance.pdf.page_24:
Article 24: 

- Regularly conduct a verification of compliance with the policy, procedures, and recommend corrective measures as necessary, 
- Provide a written opinion on new products to be commercialized and related internal control procedures, 
- Regularly provide training to all personnel on compliance control procedures related to their operations and ensure the dissemination of a culture of compliance, 
- Report to the administration body on problems and dysfunctions identified in procedures, as well as measures to be taken to address these shortcomings, and 
- Establish a semi-annual report on its activity to be transmitted to the audit committee.

TITLE VI: GOVERNANCE WITHIN BANKING GROUPS

Article 52: 

The administration body of the consolidating entity must be aware of the risks to which this entity and its subsidiaries are exposed. 

It must establish a group governance framework that clearly defines: 
- The roles and obligations of the consolidating entity and its subsidiaries, taking into account the activities and risk profile of the group, 
- Ensure the implementation of an information exchange system between group entities. 

In this regard, it must exercise appropriate surveillance of its subsidiaries while respecting the independence and autonomy of the administration body of each of its subsidiaries.

Article 53: 

The administration body of the consolidating entity must, in the exercise of its responsibilities: 
- Establish a governance framework for each subsidiary, in line with the group framework and adapted to the size of the subsidiary and the complexity of its activities, 
- Approve a group development strategy and clear policies for its implementation, 
- Define the group's global risk policy and that of its subsidiaries, 
- Approve clear policies and strategies regarding the creation of new structures and legal entities and ensure they are consistent with the group's policies and interests, 
- Implement appropriate processes and controls to detect and manage potential conflicts of interest within the group, resulting from intragroup transactions,

INTRODUCTION AND KEY  CONCEPTS  
A. BACKGROUND AND CONTE XT  
1. The risk -based approach (RBA) is central to the effective implementation of the revised FATF 
International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and 
Proliferation , which were adopted in 20121. The FATF has reviewed its  2009 RBA Guidance for 
money service businesses (MSBs), in order to bring it in line with the new FATF requirements2 and 
to reflect the experience gained by public authorities and the private sector over the years in 
                                                      
1 FATF (2012) .  
2 The FATF Standards are comprised of the  FATF Recommendations , their Interpretive Notes and 
applicable definitions from the Glossary.

4  2016  applying the RBA. This revised version applies to the money or value transfer services (MVTS)3 
sector. The FATF will also review and update its other RBA Guidance papers4 (based on the 2003 
Recommendations), to be consistent with the 2012 FATF Recommendations.  
2. The first draft of the RBA Guidance for the MVTS sector was drafted by the MVTS Project 
group, co -led by the UK and Mexico.5 Representatives of the private sector were associated with the 
work and consulted on the draft document.6 
3. The FATF adopted this updated RBA Guidance for MVTS providers at its February 2016 
Plenary.  
B. PURPOSE OF THIS GUID ANCE  
4. The purpose of this Guidance is to:  
 Support the development of a com mon understanding of what the RBA to 
AML/CFT entails for MVTS providers, banks and other financial institutions 
that maintain relationship with MVTS providers and competent authorities responsible for monitoring MVTS provider’s compliance with their AML/CFT obligations;  
 Outline the key elements involved in applying a RBA to AML/CFT associated to MVTS;  
 Highlight that financial institutions that have MVTS as customers should identify, assess and manage the ML/TF risk associated with individual MVTS, rather than avoid this category of customers;  
 Assist countries, competent authorities and MVTS providers in the design and implementation of a RBA to AML/CFT by providing general guidelines and examples of current practice;  
                                                      
3  These services are included in the FATF Glossary under “Fina ncial institutions: Money or Value 
Transfer Services (MVTS) at point 4.  
4 Between June 2007 and October 2009, the FATF adopted a set of guidance papers on the application of 
the RBA for different business sectors: financial sector, real estate agents, accountants, trust and 
company service providers (TCSPs), dealers in precious metals and stones, casinos, legal professionals, money services businesses (MSBs) and the life insurance sector:

5  The p roject group was composed of FATF -members (Spain, Switzerland, South -Africa, Singapore, Japan, 
Norway, E uropean Commission, New Zealand, United Kingdom, United States and Italy), Associate 
members  (GIABA -Secretariat, Moneyval - through Albania, APG - through Sri Lanka, GI FCS-through 
Guernsey) and Observers (World Bank, UNODC), co -led by the UK and Mexico.  
6  Comments were received from Bank of Tokyo- Mitsubishi UF J, Russian Electronic Money Association, 
MoneyGram International Inc., Mizuho Bank Ltd, Asociación de Bancos de México, Actors Federal Credit Union, Association of UK Payment Institutions, Banking Association of South Africa, European Payments Institutions Federation (EPIF), Australian Bankers' Association, Union of Arab Banks, World Savings and Retail Banking Institute/European Savings and Retail Banking Group (WSBI/ESBG), 
Canadian MSB Association, The Netherlands Association of Money transaction offices (NVG TK), 
Western Union Company and Hong Kong Association of banks (HKAB) .
